translations.literal: (Younger brother Qianheng)〉
translations.idiomatic: (His younger brother Qianheng)〉

translations.idiomatic: Xin Zixiu, Wen Chun, Zhao Shiqing, and Li Ruhua

sentences.zh: 萬士和，字思節，宜興人。

translations.literal: Wan Shihe, styled Sijie, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shihe, whose style name was Sijie, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 父吉，桐廬訓導，有學術。

translations.literal: His father Ji was an instructor in Tonglu and was learned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan Ji served as an instructor in Tonglu and was a man of scholarship.

sentences.zh: 士和成嘉靖二十年進士，改庶吉士，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Shihe passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing, was transferred to Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe passed the jinshi in the twentieth year of the Jiajing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父喪除，乞便養母，改南京兵部。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he asked to stay near his mother for convenience and was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After his period of mourning for his father, he asked to remain close to his mother for her care and was moved to the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 累遷江西僉事，歲裁上供瓷器千計。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner and each year cut imperial porcelain tribute by a thousand pieces or more.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner and each year reduced the court's porcelain tribute by more than a thousand pieces.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州提學副使，進湖廣參政。

translations.literal: He was moved to Guizhou Vice Commissioner for Education and advanced to Huguang Administration Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner for Education in Guizhou and then promoted to Administration Vice Commissioner in Huguan.

sentences.zh: 撫納叛苗二十八砦，以功賚銀幣。

translations.literal: He pacified and won over twenty-eight rebel Miao stockades and was rewarded with silver and silks for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified twenty-eight rebel Miao stockades and received silver and silks in reward.

sentences.zh: 三殿工興，采木使者旁午。

translations.literal: When construction of the Three Halls began, timber-gathering envoys came and went without pause.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the Three Halls began, envoys sent to gather timber arrived in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 士和經畫備至，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Shihe planned everything thoroughly and the people relied on him for security.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe organized the work with meticulous care, and the people were able to live in peace.

sentences.zh: 遷江西按察使，之官逾期，劾免。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Jiangxi Surveillance Commissioner; he was impeached and dismissed for arriving late to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Jiangxi Surveillance Commissioner, he was impeached and removed for exceeding the time allowed to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 起山東按察使，再行廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Surveillance Commissioner in Shandong and later served again as Left Administration Commissioner in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Surveillance Commissioner in Shandong and later served a second term as Left Administration Commissioner in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 政事故專決於左，士和曰：「朝廷設二使，如左右手，非有軒輊。」

translations.literal: Administrative business had come to be decided solely by the left commissioner. Shihe said, "The court appoints two commissioners, like the left and right hands; there is no difference in rank."
translations.idiomatic: Government affairs had come to be decided entirely by the left commissioner. Shihe said, "The court sets up two commissioners like the left and right hand—neither is higher or lower."

sentences.zh: 乃約右使分日治事。

translations.literal: He then agreed with the right commissioner to handle affairs on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: He then arranged with the right commissioner to conduct business on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 召拜應天府尹，道遷右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Prefect of Yingtian; en route he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to be Prefect of Yingtian, he was promoted en route to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 督南京糧儲，奏請便民六事。

translations.literal: He supervised Nanjing grain reserves and memorialized six measures to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: As supervisor of Nanjing grain reserves, he submitted six proposals to ease burdens on the people.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，進戶部右侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he rose to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised the granaries.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮部，進左。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and promoted to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of Rites and promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，起南京禮部侍郎，署國子監事。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong emperor acceded, Shihe was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing and acted as director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Shihe was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing and served concurrently as head of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，禮部尚書陸樹聲去位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, Minister of Rites Lu Shusheng left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli, Lu Shusheng resigned as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 張居正用樹聲言，召士和代之。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng, acting on Shusheng's recommendation, summoned Shihe to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, following Shusheng's recommendation, summoned Shihe to take his place.

sentences.zh: 條上崇儉數事。

translations.literal: He submitted several items on practicing frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a series of proposals urging frugality.

sentences.zh: 又以災祲屢見，奏乞杜幸門，容戇直，汰冗員，抑幹請，多犯時忌。

translations.literal: Because calamities recurred, he also memorialized asking to shut the door to favoritism, tolerate blunt honesty, cut redundant posts, and curb private petitions—offending many taboos of the day.
translations.idiomatic: As disasters recurred, he also asked the throne to close off avenues of favor, make room for outspoken integrity, eliminate redundant offices, and restrain private solicitations—touching many sore points of the age.

sentences.zh: 俺答及所部貢馬，邊臣請加官賞。

translations.literal: Altan and his followers presented tribute horses, and frontier officials asked for added ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Altan and his followers presented tribute horses, and border officials requested additional ranks and rewards.

sentences.zh: 士和言賞賚有成額，毋徇邊臣額外請，從之。

translations.literal: Shihe said rewards had fixed quotas and frontier officials should not be indulged in extra requests; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe argued that rewards had established quotas and border officials must not be indulged beyond them; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 方士倚馮保求官，士和持不可。

translations.literal: Daoist priests relied on Feng Bao to seek offices; Shihe firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests, leaning on Feng Bao, sought official appointments; Shihe stood firm against it.

sentences.zh: 成國公朱希忠歿，居正許贈王，士和力爭。

translations.literal: When Defender of the State Zhu Xizhong died, Juzheng agreed to ennoble him as king; Shihe argued strenuously against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Defender of the State Zhu Xizhong died, Juzheng agreed to grant him a royal title; Shihe fought the decision hard.

sentences.zh: 給事中余懋學言事得罪，士和言直臣不當斥。

translations.literal: When Supervising Secretary Yu Maoxue was punished for remonstrating, Shihe said upright officials should not be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Yu Maoxue was punished for speaking out, Shihe argued that straightforward ministers should not be cast out.

sentences.zh: 於是積忤居正。

translations.literal: Thus he accumulated offenses against Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he steadily offended Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱南雍承風劾之，遂謝病去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhu Nanyong, taking his cue, impeached him, and Shihe resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Nanyong, following the prevailing wind, impeached him, and Shihe resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，起南京禮部尚書，再疏引年不赴。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, Shihe was recalled as Minister of Rites at Nanjing but twice asked to retire on account of age and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was recalled as Minister of Rites at Nanjing but twice pleaded age and did not go.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚文恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 王之誥，字告若，石首人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhigao, styled Gaoruo, was a native of Shishou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhigao, whose style name was Gaoruo, came from Shishou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授吉水知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部主事，改兵部員外郎，出為河南僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, then to an outside post as Assistant Commissioner in Henan after serving as an outside secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, became an outside secretary in the Ministry of War, and was then posted as Assistant Commissioner in Henan.

sentences.zh: 討師尚詔有功，轉參議。

translations.literal: He had merit in suppressing Shi Shangzhao and was promoted to Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He earned merit suppressing Shi Shangzhao and was promoted to Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 調大同兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Datong.

sentences.zh: 以搗板升功，增俸一級，進山西右參政，擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: For merit in raiding the Barbarian Ascendant, his salary was raised one grade; he advanced to Right Administration Vice Commissioner in Shanxi, was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and became Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in raiding the Barbarian Ascendant faction, his salary was raised one grade; he became Right Administration Vice Commissioner in Shanxi, was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 大興屯田，每營墾田百五十頃，役軍四百人。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded garrison farming: each camp reclaimed one hundred fifty qing, employing four hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded military colonies: each camp reclaimed one hundred fifty qing of land with four hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 列上便宜八事，行之。

translations.literal: He listed eight expedient measures and they were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted eight practical measures, and they were implemented.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋以左侍郎總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: Soon, as Left Vice Minister, he was made supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as Left Vice Minister, he was appointed supreme commander of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，就進右都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was promoted on the spot to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he was promoted on the spot to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 俺答犯石州，之誥令山西總兵官申維嶽、參將劉寶、尤月、黑雲龍四營兵尾之南下，而檄大同總兵官孫吳、山西副總兵田世威等出天門關，遏其東歸。

translations.literal: When Altan attacked Shizhou, Zhigao ordered Shanxi Commander-in-Chief Shen Weiyue and the battalion commanders Liu Bao, You Yue, and Hei Yunlong to follow the raiders south, while dispatching Datong Commander-in-Chief Sun Wu, Shanxi Deputy Commander Tian Shiwei, and others through Tianmen Pass to block their return east.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan attacked Shizhou, Zhigao ordered Shanxi Commander-in-Chief Shen Weiyue and Battalion Commanders Liu Bao, You Yue, and Hei Yunlong to trail the invaders south, while instructing Datong Commander Sun Wu, Shanxi Deputy Commander Tian Shiwei, and others to march out through Tianmen Pass and cut off their retreat eastward.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王繼洛駐代州不出，維嶽不敢前，石州遂陷。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Jiluo remained at Daizhou and would not advance; Weiyue did not dare move forward, and Shizhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Jiluo stayed at Daizhou and would not come out; Weiyue dared not advance, and Shizhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 殺人數萬，所過無孑遺，大掠十有四日而去。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands were killed; nothing living was left where they passed, and after fourteen days of great plunder they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands were slaughtered; wherever they passed not a soul remained, and after fourteen days of wholesale looting they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 事聞，維嶽、世威、寶論死，繼洛戍邊，吳落職。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Weiyue, Shiwei, and Bao were sentenced to death, Jiluo was banished to the frontier, and Wu was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Weiyue, Shiwei, and Bao were condemned to death, Jiluo was sent to border service, and Wu was demoted.

sentences.zh: 之誥以還守南山，止貶二秩。

translations.literal: Zhigao, because he had held the line at Nanshan on the return, was only demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao, credited with holding Nanshan on the enemy's withdrawal, was merely demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔之誥以左侍郎巡視薊、遼、保定、宣、大、山西，侍郎劉燾巡陜西、延綏、寧夏、甘肅。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered Zhigao, as Left Vice Minister, to inspect Ji, Liaodong, Baoding, Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi, and Vice Minister Liu Tao to inspect Shaanxi, Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict named Zhigao, as Left Vice Minister, to inspect Ji, Liaodong, Baoding, Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi, and Vice Minister Liu Tao to inspect Shaanxi, Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 之誥以疾辭，代以冀練。

translations.literal: Zhigao pleaded illness and declined; Ji Lian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao declined on grounds of illness and Ji Lian took his place.

sentences.zh: 已，復因給事中張鹵言，皆罷不遣。

translations.literal: Later, on the remonstrance of Supervising Secretary Zhang Lu, both appointments were cancelled and neither was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Supervising Secretary Zhang Lu's memorial, both appointments were revoked and neither man was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 三年，起督京營。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled to command the capital garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to command the metropolitan garrisons.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史，總督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made supreme commander of the three frontiers in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Censor-in-Chief and was made supreme commander of Shaanxi's three frontiers.

sentences.zh: 以延寧將士搗巢功，予一子官，遷南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: For the merit of Yan-Ning troops in raiding enemy nests, one of his sons was granted office; he was transferred to Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: For the merit of Yan-Ning troops in storming enemy strongholds, one son was granted office, and he was moved to Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong emperor succeeded, Zhigao was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, Zhigao was summoned as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 張居正專政，之誥與有連，每規切之。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng held sole power; Zhigao was connected with him yet often admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng monopolized government; Zhigao was related to him by marriage yet repeatedly urged restraint upon him.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三年，乞假送母歸，逾時不至，被劾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli he asked leave to escort his mother home and, when he failed to return on time, was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wanli he asked leave to take his mother home and, when he overstayed, was impeached.

sentences.zh: 會之誥亦奏請終養，遂報許。

translations.literal: Zhigao also memorialized asking to complete his mourning, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zhigao asked to remain in mourning, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 後居正喪父奪情，杖言者闕下。

translations.literal: Later, when Juzheng's father died and he was ordered to remain at his post, he had remonstrators beaten at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Juzheng's father died and he was ordered to remain in office rather than mourn, he had remonstrators flogged below the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 歸葬還闕，之誥以召還直臣收人心為勸。

translations.literal: After the burial, on his return to court, Zhigao urged him to recall upright officials in order to win hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng returned from the burial, Zhigao urged him to recall straightforward officials and recover popular goodwill.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚端襄。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Duanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the title Duanxiang.

sentences.zh: 時有夷陵劉一儒者，字孟真，亦居正姻也。

translations.literal: At the time there was Liu Yiru of Yiling, styled Mengzhen, who was also related to Juzheng by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Liu Yiru of Yiling, styled Mengzhen, who was likewise connected to Juzheng by marriage.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 屢官刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly held office as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 居正當國，嘗貽書規之。

translations.literal: While Juzheng was in power, he once sent him a letter of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: While Juzheng held power, he once wrote him a letter of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，親黨皆坐斥，一儒獨以高潔名。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, his kin were all punished and dismissed; Yiru alone was known for lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death his kin were all punished and dismissed; Yiru alone was famed for lofty integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋拜南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 甫半歲，移疾歸。

translations.literal: After only half a year he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After only half a year he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 初，居正女歸一儒子，珠琲紈綺盈箱篋，一儒悉扃之別室。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Juzheng's daughter married Yiru's son, pearls, jade, and silks filled chests and boxes; Yiru locked them all in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Juzheng's daughter married Yiru's son, pearls, jade, and silks filled chests and boxes; Yiru sealed them all in a separate chamber.

sentences.zh: 居正死，貲產盡入官，一儒乃發向所緘物還之。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died his property was confiscated; Yiru then opened what he had sealed and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng died his property was confiscated; Yiru then opened what he had sealed and returned it all.

sentences.zh: 南京御史李一陽請還一儒於朝，以厲恬讓。

translations.literal: Nanjing Censor Li Yiyang asked that Yiru be recalled to court to encourage modest restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Censor Li Yiyang asked that Yiru be recalled to court as a model of modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 一儒竟不赴召，卒於家。

translations.literal: Yiru never answered the summons and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Yiru never answered the summons and died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，追謚莊介。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 吳百朋，字維錫，義烏人。

translations.literal: Wu Baipeng, styled Weixi, was a native of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Baipeng, whose style name was Weixi, came from Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六主年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授永豐知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 徵拜御史，歷按淮、揚、湖廣。

translations.literal: He was summoned as censor and successively inspected Huai, Yang, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as censor and in turn inspected Huai, Yang, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 擢大理寺丞，進右少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and advanced to Right Vice Minister of the same court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and then to Right Vice Minister of the same court.

sentences.zh: 四十二年夏，進右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the summer of the forty-second year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and pacified Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the forty-second year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 改提督軍務，巡撫南、贛、汀、漳。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner-in-Chief of Military Affairs and Grand Coordinator of Nan, Gan, Ting, and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Commissioner-in-Chief of Military Affairs and Grand Coordinator of Nan, Gan, Ting, and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 與兩廣提督吳桂芳討平河源賊李亞元、程鄉賊葉丹樓，又會師破倭海豐。

translations.literal: With Guangdong Commissioner-in-Chief Wu Guifang he suppressed the Heyuan bandit Li Yayuan and the Chengxiang bandit Ye Danlou, and jointly broke the pirates at Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Guangdong Commissioner-in-Chief Wu Guifang he put down the Heyuan bandit Li Yayuan and the Chengxiang bandit Ye Danlou, and jointly destroyed the pirates at Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 初，廣東大埔民藍松山、余大眷倡亂，流劫潼、延、興、泉間。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lan Songshan and Yu Dajuan of Dapu in Guangdong had raised rebellion and raided through Tong, Yan, Xing, and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lan Songshan and Yu Dajuan of Dapu in Guangdong had stirred rebellion and raided through Tong, Yan, Xing, and Quan.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊敗之，奔永春。

translations.literal: Government troops defeated them and they fled to Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops defeated them and they fled to Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 與香寮盜蘇阿普、範繼祖連兵犯德化，為都指揮耿宗元所敗，偽請撫。

translations.literal: They joined with the Xiangliao bandits Su Apu and Fan Jizu to attack Dehua, were defeated by Regional Commander Geng Zongyuan, and falsely asked for pacification.
translations.idiomatic: They joined the Xiangliao bandits Su Apu and Fan Jizu in attacking Dehua, were defeated by Regional Commander Geng Zongyuan, and pretended to seek pacification.

sentences.zh: 百朋亦陽罷兵，而誘賊黨為內應，先後悉擒之，惟三巢未下。

translations.literal: Baipeng also feigned a halt to fighting while enticing traitors within the band as inside agents; in time he captured them all, though three nests remained untaken.
translations.idiomatic: Baipeng likewise feigned a cease-fire while turning bandit sympathizers into informants; one after another he captured them all, though three strongholds still held out.

sentences.zh: 三巢者，和平李文彪據岑岡，龍南謝允樟據高沙，賴清規據下歷。

translations.literal: The three nests were: Li Wenbiao of Heping holding Cengang, Xie Yunzhang of Longnan holding Gaosha, and Lai Qinggui holding Xialü.
translations.idiomatic: The three strongholds were Li Wenbiao of Heping at Cengang, Xie Yunzhang of Longnan at Gaosha, and Lai Qinggui at Xialü.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以倭患棘，不討且十年。

translations.literal: The court, harried by Japanese raids, had not campaigned against them for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: With Japanese raids pressing hard, the court had left them unpunished for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 文彪死，子珍及江月照繼之，益猖獗。

translations.literal: When Wenbiao died, his son Zhen and Jiang Yuezhao succeeded him and grew all the more violent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbiao died, his son Zhen and Jiang Yuezhao took his place and grew still more violent.

sentences.zh: 四十四年秋，百朋進右副都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the forty-fourth year Baipeng was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief while remaining Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the forty-fourth year Baipeng rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and continued as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「三巢僭號稱王，旋撫旋叛。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The three nests usurp titles and call themselves kings, accepting pacification one moment and rebelling the next.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The three strongholds have taken royal titles; they accept pacification and rebel again in turn.

sentences.zh: 廣東和平、龍川、興寧，江西龍南、信豐、安遠，蠶食過半。

translations.literal: In Guangdong, Heping, Longchuan, and Xingning, and in Jiangxi, Longnan, Xinfeng, and Anyuan, they had nibbled away more than half the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Across Heping, Longchuan, and Xingning in Guangdong and Longnan, Xinfeng, and Anyuan in Jiangxi, they had swallowed more than half the districts.

sentences.zh: 不亟討，禍不可言。

translations.literal: If they are not attacked at once, disaster is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they are crushed quickly, the harm will be beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 三巢中惟清規跨江、廣六縣，最逆命，用兵必自下歷始。」

translations.literal: Among the three nests only Qinggui, spanning six counties in Jiang and Guang, was most defiant; military action had to begin at Xialü."
translations.idiomatic: Of the three strongholds only Qinggui, whose reach crossed six counties in Jiangxi and Guangdong, was the most rebellious; force must begin at Xialü."

sentences.zh: 帝采部義，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted the ministry's view and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the ministry's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 百朋乃命守備蔡汝蘭討擒清規於苦竹嶂，群賊震懾。

translations.literal: Baipeng then ordered Garrison Commander Cai Rulan to attack and capture Qinggui at Kuzhu Ridge, and the bandits were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Baipeng ordered Garrison Commander Cai Rulan to capture Qinggui at Kuzhu Ridge, and the bandits were struck with fear.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，吏部以百朋積苦兵間，稍遷大理卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing the Ministry of Personnel, noting Baipeng's long hardship in war, moved him slightly to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing the Ministry of Personnel, seeing how worn Baipeng was by campaigning, transferred him to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 給事中歐陽一敬等請留百朋剿賊，詔進兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Ouyang Yijing and others asked that Baipeng be kept to suppress bandits; an edict promoted him to Right Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief while he remained Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Ouyang Yijing and others asked that Baipeng stay to fight bandits; an edict made him Right Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief with his grand coordinator title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 百朋奏，春夏用兵妨耕作，宜且聽撫，帝從之。

translations.literal: Baipeng memorialized that campaigning in spring and summer would harm farming and that pacification should be heard for the time being; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Baipeng argued that spring and summer campaigns would disrupt planting and that pacification should be tried for now; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 乞終養，不許。

translations.literal: He asked to retire and care for his parents to the end; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to remain home and complete his filial mourning; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 改刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Right Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸，起改兵部。

translations.literal: When his father died he went home; on recall he was changed to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he returned home; when recalled he was placed in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，奉命閱視宣、大、山西三鎮。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli he was ordered to inspect the three garrisons of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he was ordered to inspect Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 百朋以糧餉、險隘、兵馬、器械、屯田、鹽法、番馬、逆黨八事核邊臣，督撫王崇古、吳兌、總兵郭琥以下，升賞黜革有差。

translations.literal: Baipeng used eight matters—grain pay, passes, horses and men, weapons, garrison farms, salt law, tribute horses, and rebel factions—to audit frontier officials; Grand Coordinators Wang Chonggu and Wu Dui, Commander-in-Chief Guo Hu, and those below were promoted, rewarded, dismissed, or demoted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Baipeng reviewed frontier officials on eight points—supplies, defiles, troops and horses, arms, military colonies, salt regulations, tribute horses, and rebel parties—and Wang Chonggu, Wu Dui, Guo Hu, and the rest were rewarded or punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又進邊圖，凡關塞險隘，番族部落，士馬強弱，亭障遠近，歷歷如指掌。

translations.literal: He also submitted a frontier map on which every pass, barbarian tribe, strength of men and horses, and distance of beacon towers was as clear as the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented a frontier map on which every pass, tribal settlement, troop strength, and beacon distance stood out as plainly as lines on the palm.

sentences.zh: 以省母歸。

translations.literal: He returned home to visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to see his mother.

sentences.zh: 起南京右都御史，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, he was soon summoned as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 劉應節，字子和，濰人。

translations.literal: Liu Yingjie, styled Zihe, was a native of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yingjie, whose style name was Zihe, came from Wei county.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷井陘兵備副使，兼轄三關。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Jingxing and concurrently controlled the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Jingxing and took charge of the Three Passes as well.

sentences.zh: 三關屬井陘道自此始。

translations.literal: From this time the Three Passes came under the Jingxing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Three Passes were placed under the Jingxing circuit.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，以山西右參政擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, as Right Administration Vice Commissioner in Shanxi he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and became Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, as Right Administration Vice Commissioner in Shanxi, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 母喪歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，起撫河南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to pacify Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to serve as Grand Coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 俺答寇石州，山西騷動，詔應節赴援。

translations.literal: When Altan raided Shizhou and Shanxi was in turmoil, an edict ordered Yingjie to go to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan attacked Shizhou and Shanxi was thrown into alarm, Yingjie was ordered to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 已，寇退。

translations.literal: Soon the raiders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會順天巡撫耿隨卿坐殺平民充首功逮治，改應節代之。

translations.literal: At the same time Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing of Shuntian was arrested for killing commoners to claim first merit; Yingjie replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing of Shuntian was arrested for killing civilians to claim top credit; Yingjie took his place.

sentences.zh: 建議永平西門抵海口距天津止五百里，可通漕，請募民習海道者赴天津領運，同運官出海達永平。

translations.literal: He proposed that from Yongping's west gate to the sea mouth was only five hundred li from Tianjin and grain transport could pass; he asked to recruit men skilled on the sea to receive shipments at Tianjin and sail with transport officials to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Yongping's west gate lay only five hundred li from the sea mouth at Tianjin and could be linked to the grain route, and asked to recruit seafaring men to take grain at Tianjin and sail with transport officials to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 部議以漕卒冒險不便，發山東、河南粟十萬石儲天津，令永平官民自運焉。

translations.literal: The ministry decided that grain soldiers should not be risked at sea; instead one hundred thousand shi of grain from Shandong and Henan were stored at Tianjin for Yongping officials and people to transport themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that grain troops should not be sent to sea; instead one hundred thousand shi from Shandong and Henan were stored at Tianjin for Yongping to haul overland.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，進右副都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief while remaining Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and kept his coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 旋進兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，代譚綸總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, replacing Tan Lun as supreme commander of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, replacing Tan Lun as supreme commander of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 奏罷永平、密雲、霸州采礦。

translations.literal: He memorialized to stop mining at Yongping, Miyun, and Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to halt mining at Yongping, Miyun, and Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 又因御史傅孟春言，議諸鎮積貯，當計歲豐歉。

translations.literal: On the remonstrance of Censor Fu Mengchun he also discussed garrison stores and said yearly abundance or shortage should be calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Following Censor Fu Mengchun he also discussed frontier reserves and said stores should be planned according to whether the year was plentiful or lean.

sentences.zh: 常時以折色便軍，可以積粟；

translations.literal: In normal years commutation payments could ease the army and grain could be stored;
translations.idiomatic: In good years payments in silver could ease the troops and grain could be accumulated;

sentences.zh: 兇歲以本色濟荒，可以積銀。

translations.literal: in famine years grain in kind could relieve distress and silver could be stored.
translations.idiomatic: in bad years grain in kind could relieve famine and silver could be saved.

sentences.zh: 又明年建議通漕密雲，上疏曰：「密雲環控潮、白二水，天設之以便漕者也。

translations.literal: The next year he proposed opening grain transport to Miyun and memorialized: "Miyun is ringed by the Chao and Bai rivers—heaven made it for transport.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he proposed extending the canal to Miyun and wrote: "Miyun is embraced by the Chao and Bai rivers; nature meant it for transport.

sentences.zh: 向二水分流，到牛欄山始合。

translations.literal: Formerly the two streams divided and only joined at Niulan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the two rivers split and met only at Niulan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 通州運艘至牛欄山，以上陸運至龍慶倉，輸挽甚苦。

translations.literal: Transport barges from Tongzhou reached Niulan Mountain and above that grain went by land to Longqing granary, with painful hauling.
translations.idiomatic: Barges from Tongzhou went to Niulan Mountain; above that point grain was hauled overland to Longqing granary at great cost.

sentences.zh: 今白水徙流城西，去潮水不二百武，近且疏渠植壩，合為一流，水深漕便。

translations.literal: Now the Bai had shifted west of the city, less than two hundred bu from the tidal river; if channels and dams were dredged and joined into one stream, the water would be deep and transport easy.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Bai had shifted west of the city, within two hundred paces of the tidal river; dredging channels and building dams to unite the streams would deepen the water and ease transport.

sentences.zh: 舊昌平運額共十八萬石有奇，今止十四萬，密雲僅得十萬，惟賴召商一法，而地瘠民貧，勢難長恃。

translations.literal: The old Changping quota was more than one hundred eighty thousand shi; now only one hundred forty thousand remained, and Miyun received only one hundred thousand, relying solely on merchant contracting—yet the land was poor and the people impoverished, a policy hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Changping's old quota exceeded one hundred eighty thousand shi; now only one hundred forty thousand were delivered, and Miyun received only one hundred thousand, depending entirely on hired merchants—yet the region was poor and could not rely on that forever.

sentences.zh: 聞通倉粟多紅朽。

translations.literal: It was heard that grain in Tong granary was much spoiled.
translations.idiomatic: He heard that much grain in Tong granary had rotted.

sentences.zh: 若漕五萬石於密雲，而以本鎮折色三萬五千兩留給京軍，則通倉無腐粟，京軍沾實惠，密雲免僉商，一舉而三善備矣。」

translations.literal: If fifty thousand shi were transported to Miyun while the garrison's commuted silver of thirty-five thousand taels were kept for the capital army, Tong granary would have no rotten grain, the capital troops would gain real benefit, and Miyun would be freed from forced merchants—three goods in one act."
translations.idiomatic: If fifty thousand shi were shipped to Miyun while the garrison's thirty-five thousand taels in commuted silver were kept for the capital army, Tong would lose no spoiled grain, the capital troops would benefit, Miyun would escape forced merchants, and three aims would be met at once."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳渠以薊鎮多虛伍，請核兵省餉。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Qu, noting many phantom rolls in the Ji garrison, asked to audit troops and save pay.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Qu, noting many empty rolls in the Ji garrison, asked to verify troops and cut expenses.

sentences.zh: 應節上疏曰：「國初設立大寧，薊門猶稱內地。

translations.literal: Yingjie memorialized: "When the dynasty first established Daning, the Ji frontier was still called inner territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjie wrote: "When the dynasty first set up Daning, the Ji passes were still treated as inner country.

sentences.zh: 既大寧內徙，三衛反覆，一切防禦之計，與宣、大相埒，而額兵不滿三萬。

translations.literal: After Daning was moved inward and the three guards turned treacherous, every defensive plan matched Xuan and Da, yet allotted troops fell short of thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Daning was withdrawn inland and the three guards wavered, every defense matched Xuanfu and Datong, yet allotted troops numbered less than thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 倉卒召外兵，疲於奔命，又半孱弱。

translations.literal: Hurriedly calling outside troops tired them with running to and fro, and half were weak.
translations.idiomatic: Calling in outside troops at every alarm exhausted them on the march, and half were feeble.

sentences.zh: 於是議減客兵，募土著，而遊食之徒，饑聚飽飏。

translations.literal: Then they debated cutting guest troops and recruiting locals, while wandering idlers gathered when hungry and scattered when full.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to cut outside troops and recruit locals followed, while vagrants flocked when hungry and scattered when fed.

sentences.zh: 請清勾逃軍，而所勾皆老稚，又未必安於其伍。

translations.literal: They asked to clear deserters, yet those found were old and young who might not settle in their units.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed hunting down deserters, yet those caught were often old or young and ill-suited to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 本鎮西起鎮邊，東抵山海，因地制兵，非三十萬不可。

translations.literal: This garrison runs from Zhenbian in the west to Shanhai in the east; troops must be tailored to terrain, and no fewer than three hundred thousand are needed.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison runs from Zhenbian west to Shanhai east; troops must fit the ground, and three hundred thousand are required.

sentences.zh: 今主、客兵不過十三萬而已。

translations.literal: Now resident and guest troops together number only a little more than one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Today resident and outside troops together barely exceed one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 且宣府地方六百里，額兵十五萬；

translations.literal: Xuanfu covers six hundred li with fifteen thousand allotted troops;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu spans six hundred li with fifteen thousand allotted troops;

sentences.zh: 大同地方千餘里，額兵十三萬五千；

translations.literal: Datong covers more than a thousand li with one hundred thirty-five thousand allotted troops;
translations.idiomatic: Datong spans more than a thousand li with one hundred thirty-five thousand allotted troops;

sentences.zh: 今薊、昌地兼二鎮，而兵力獨不足。

translations.literal: now Ji and Chang combine the territory of both garrisons yet their strength alone is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Chang together cover both territories yet their forces alone are not enough.

sentences.zh: 援彼例此，何以能守？

translations.literal: Applying those examples here, how can the frontier be held?
translations.idiomatic: If we measure by those examples, how can we defend the line?

sentences.zh: 以今上計，發精兵二十余萬，恢復大寧，控制外邊，俾畿輔肩背益厚，宣、遼聲援相通，國有重關，庭無近寇，此萬年之利也。

translations.literal: On the highest plan, send more than two hundred thousand elite troops, recover Daning, control the outer marches, thicken the capital's shoulders, link Xuan and Liao in mutual support, give the state a second barrier, and keep raiders far from court—profit for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The best course is to send over two hundred thousand crack troops, recover Daning, control the outer frontier, thicken the capital's defenses, link Xuanfu and Liaodong, set a second barrier for the state, and keep enemies far from the throne—a gain for ages.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，集兵三十萬，分屯列戍，使首尾相應，此百年之利也。

translations.literal: If not, gather three hundred thousand troops in garrisons so head and tail respond—profit for a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: If not, station three hundred thousand men in linked posts so the line answers from end to end—a gain for a century.

sentences.zh: 又不然，則選主、客兵十七萬，訓練有成，不必仰藉鄰鎮，亦目前茍安之計。

translations.literal: If not again, choose one hundred seventy thousand resident and guest troops, train them well, and need not lean on neighboring garrisons—a plan for present peace at least.
translations.idiomatic: A third course is to pick one hundred seventy thousand resident and outside troops, train them properly, and stop relying on neighboring garrisons—a makeshift for the moment.

sentences.zh: 今皆不然，征兵如弈棋，請餉如乞糴，操練如摶沙，教戰如談虎。

translations.literal: Now none of these is done: calling troops is like moving chess pieces, begging funds like begging grain, drilling like clutching sand, teaching battle like talking of tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Today none of this is done: troops are moved like chessmen, funds begged like alms, drill is sand in the hand, and battle practice is talk of tigers.

sentences.zh: 邊長兵寡，掣襟肘見。

translations.literal: The frontier is long and troops few; sleeves are pulled and elbows show.
translations.idiomatic: The line is long and soldiers few; every move exposes a weakness.

sentences.zh: 今為不得已之計，姑勾新軍補主兵舊額十一萬，與入衛客兵分番休息，庶軍不告勞，稍定邊計。」

translations.literal: As an unavoidable measure, for now clear new troops to fill the old resident quota of one hundred ten thousand and let capital guest troops rotate in rest, so the army is not worn out and the frontier may settle somewhat."
translations.idiomatic: For now, as a last resort, fill the old resident quota of one hundred ten thousand with new recruits and rotate capital guest troops in relief, so troops are not exhausted and the border may steady somewhat."

sentences.zh: 部議行所司清軍，而補兵之說卒不行。

translations.literal: The ministry ordered the offices to clear troops, but the plan to fill ranks was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ordered a troop audit, but the plan to refill the ranks was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，進右都御史兼兵部右侍郎，總督如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Right Vice Minister of War while remaining supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli he became Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Right Vice Minister of War with his command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 進南京工部尚書，召為戎政尚書，改刑部。

translations.literal: He advanced to Minister of Works at Nanjing, was summoned as Minister of Military Administration, and was changed to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Works at Nanjing, was summoned as Minister of Military Administration, and was moved to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 錦衣馮邦寧者，太監保從子，道遇不引避，應節叱下之，保不悅。

translations.literal: The brocade guard officer Feng Bangning, nephew of eunuch Feng Bao, failed to step aside when they met on the road; Yingjie had him pulled down, and Bao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bangning of the Brocade Guard, a nephew of eunuch Feng Bao, did not yield on the road; Yingjie had him seized, and Bao took offense.

sentences.zh: 會雲南參政羅汝芳奉表至京，應節出郭與談禪，給事中周良寅疏論之，遂偕汝芳劾罷。

translations.literal: When Yunnan Administration Vice Commissioner Luo Rufang came to court with a memorial, Yingjie went outside the city to discuss Chan with him; Supervising Secretary Zhou Liangyin memorialized against this, and both were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Rufang of Yunnan arrived with a tribute memorial, Yingjie met him outside the walls to discuss Chan; Supervising Secretary Zhou Liangyin attacked this, and both Yingjie and Luo were impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，王宗沐建議海運，應節與工部侍郎徐栻請開膠萊河，張居正力主之。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Zongmu had proposed sea transport; Yingjie and Vice Minister of Works Xu Shi asked to open the Jiao-Lai Canal, and Zhang Juzheng strongly supported it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Zongmu had urged sea transport; Yingjie and Vice Minister Xu Shi proposed opening the Jiao-Lai Canal, which Zhang Juzheng strongly backed.

sentences.zh: 用栻樣兼僉都御史以往，議鑿山引泉，計費百萬。

translations.literal: Xu Shi was sent as Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief to oversee the work; they planned to cut mountains and draw springs at a cost of one million.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shi went out as Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief; they planned to cut through mountains and channel springs at a cost of one million taels.

sentences.zh: 議者爭駁之。

translations.literal: Memorialists disputed it heatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued fiercely against it.

sentences.zh: 召式還，罷其役。

translations.literal: Shi was recalled and the project halted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was recalled and the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 栻，常熟人，累官南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Changshu and rose to Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, a native of Changshu, eventually became Minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 王遴，字繼津，霸州人。

translations.literal: Wang Lin, styled Jijin, was a native of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin, whose style name was Jijin, came from Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除紹興推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部主事，歷員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the Ministry of War as principal secretary and rose to outside secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of War as principal secretary and rose to outside secretary.

sentences.zh: 峭直矜節概，不妄交。

translations.literal: Upright, stern, and mindful of integrity, he did not make friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and principled and did not form friendships lightly.

sentences.zh: 同官楊繼盛劾嚴嵩及其孫效忠冒功事，下部覆。

translations.literal: His colleague Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and his grandson for falsely claiming merit; the case went to the ministry for review.
translations.idiomatic: Colleague Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and his grandson for feigning merit; the ministry was ordered to review the case.

sentences.zh: 世蕃自為稿，以屬武選郎中周冕。

translations.literal: Shifan himself drafted a reply and gave it to Selection Director Zhou Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan drafted his own reply and handed it to Selection Director Zhou Mian.

sentences.zh: 冕發之，反得罪。

translations.literal: Mian made it public and was punished in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Mian exposed the draft and was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 尚書聶豹懼，趣所司以世蕃稿上。

translations.literal: Minister Nie Bao was afraid and urged the office to submit Shifan's draft.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Nie Bao, afraid, pressed the office to file Shifan's version.

sentences.zh: 遴直前爭，豹怒，竟覆如世蕃言。

translations.literal: Lin stepped forward to argue; Bao was angry, and the review followed Shifan after all.
translations.idiomatic: Lin protested face to face; Bao grew angry, and the finding followed Shifan anyway.

sentences.zh: 繼盛論死，遴為資粥饘，且以女字其子應箕。

translations.literal: When Jisheng was sentenced to death, Lin supplied him porridge and gruel and betrothed his daughter to Jisheng's son Yingji.
translations.idiomatic: When Jisheng was condemned to death, Lin brought him food and betrothed his daughter to Jisheng's son Yingji.

sentences.zh: 嵩父子大恚，摭他事下之詔獄。

translations.literal: The Song father and son were furious and found other charges to send him to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were enraged and found other charges to throw him into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 事白復官。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was cleared he was restored.

sentences.zh: 及繼盛死，收葬之。

translations.literal: After Jisheng died he gathered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jisheng died he collected the body and buried him.

sentences.zh: 遷山東僉事，再遷岢嵐兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Commissioner in Shandong and then to Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Kelan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Assistant Commissioner in Shandong and then Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Kelan.

sentences.zh: 有威名，為巡撫所忌，劾去。

translations.literal: He had a fierce reputation and was envied by the grand coordinator, who impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: He won a stern reputation; the grand coordinator resented him and had him impeached out of office.

sentences.zh: 官民相率訟冤，詔許起用。

translations.literal: Officials and people together petitioned his innocence, and an edict allowed his recall.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners together pleaded his case, and an edict permitted his reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and became Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and became Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 寇大入定邊、固原，總兵官郭江戰歿。

translations.literal: Bandits greatly entered Dingbian and Guyuan and Commander-in-Chief Guo Jiang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders poured into Dingbian and Guyuan and Commander Guo Jiang was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 總督陳其學、陜西巡撫戴才坐免，遴貶俸一秩。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue and Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Dai Cai were dismissed; Lin's salary was cut one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue and Grand Coordinator Dai Cai were removed; Lin's salary was reduced one grade.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，寇六入塞，皆失利去。

translations.literal: When Longqing began, raiders entered the passes six times and each time withdrew defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longqing raiders crossed the border six times and each time retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 而御史溫如玉論遴不已，解官候勘。

translations.literal: Yet Censor Wen Ruyu kept attacking Lin, and he was relieved pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Censor Wen Ruyu kept impeaching him, and he was suspended pending review.

sentences.zh: 後御史楊鉁勘上其功，遂以故官巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: Later Censor Yang Zhen investigated and upheld his merit, and he was sent back to his old post as Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Censor Yang Zhen reviewed the case and affirmed his merit, and he returned as Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 總兵官馬芳驍勇，寇不敢深入。

translations.literal: The regional commander Ma Fang was brave in battle, and the bandits did not dare go deep.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Ma Fang was so fierce that the raiders dared not press far inland.

sentences.zh: 遴乃大興屯田，邊儲賴之。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon greatly promoted garrison farming, and the frontier stores relied upon this.
translations.idiomatic: Lin then greatly expanded military colonies, on which frontier grain reserves came to depend.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 省親歸，起協理戎政。

translations.literal: After returning from visiting his parents, he was raised up to assist in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After going home on leave to see his parents, he was recalled to assist in military administration.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，張居正秉政。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended, Zhang Juzheng held government power.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, Zhang Juzheng took charge of the government.

sentences.zh: 遴其同年生，然雅不相能。

translations.literal: Lin was his fellow examination-year graduate, yet they ordinarily were not compatible.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was his fellow graduate of the same year, but the two were never on good terms.

sentences.zh: 會議閱邊，遴請行。

translations.literal: When there was a conference to inspect the frontier, Lin requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated an inspection tour of the frontier, Lin volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 命往陜西四鎮。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to the four garrisons of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to the four Shaanxi defense commands.

sentences.zh: 峻絕饋遺。

translations.literal: He sternly rejected gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He flatly refused all gifts and gratuities.

sentences.zh: 事竣，遽移疾歸。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, he suddenly pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once his mission was complete, he abruptly pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，始起南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, only then was he raised as Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Juzheng's death was he recalled as Nanjing Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to the Ministry of War, assisting in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 守備中官丘得用濫役營軍，遴奏禁之，因奏行計安留都十二事。

translations.literal: The eunuch garrison commander Qiu Deyong wantonly impressed camp troops for labor; Lin memorialized to forbid this, and furthermore memorialized to implement twelve measures to secure the southern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch defender Qiu Deyong pressed garrison troops into illicit service; Lin memorialized against this and proposed twelve measures to stabilize the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to serve as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 先奉詔蠲除及織造議留共銀百七十六萬余兩，命於太倉庫補進，遴言：「陛下歷十余年之儲積，僅三百余萬，今因一載蠲除，即收補於庫。

translations.literal: Previously, by imperial order, remissions and weaving-manufacture funds held back totaled more than 1,760,000 taels of silver; it was ordered that they be made up from the Taicang treasury. Lin said: 'Your Majesty has accumulated over more than ten years a reserve of only a little over 3,000,000; now because of remissions in one year, it is immediately to be recovered into the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The court had earlier ordered remissions and retained weaving funds totaling more than 1.76 million taels of silver, with instructions to replenish the Taicang vault; Lin argued: 'Your Majesty has built up reserves over more than a decade to barely three million taels; now a single year of remissions would be offset by immediate recovery into the treasury.

sentences.zh: 計十余年之積，不足償二年取補之資。

translations.literal: Calculated, the accumulation of more than ten years is insufficient to repay the funds taken and made up over two years.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years of accumulation would not even cover what must be drawn and replenished in two.

sentences.zh: 矧金花額進歲當百萬，自六年以後增進二十萬，今合六年計之，不啻百萬矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the annual quota payment of golden-flower silver should be one million; since the sixth year an additional two hundred thousand has been added; now counting six years together, it is no less than one million.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the annual golden-flower quota already runs to one million taels; since the sixth year another two hundred thousand have been added—over six years that comes to well over a million.

sentences.zh: 庫積非源泉，歲進不已，後將何繼？」

translations.literal: Treasury accumulation is not a spring source; yearly payments unceasing—what will follow after?"
translations.idiomatic: The vault is not an inexhaustible spring; if annual intake never stops increasing, what will sustain it later?"

sentences.zh: 因言京、通二倉糧積八百萬石，足供九年之需，請量改折百五十萬石，三年而止。

translations.literal: He therefore spoke: the grain stored in the Jing and Tong granaries totals eight million shi, sufficient for nine years' need; he requested converting in measure one million five hundred thousand shi, stopping after three years.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say that the Jing and Tong granaries held eight million shi of grain, enough for nine years, and urged commutation of 1.5 million shi for a period of three years only.

sentences.zh: 詔許一年。

translations.literal: An edict permitted one year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved only one year.

sentences.zh: 時尚寶丞徐貞明、御史徐待開京東水田，遴力贊之，議遂決。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Master of the Privy Treasury Xu Zhenming and Censor Xu Dai proposed opening paddy fields east of the capital; Lin strongly supported it, and the proposal was decided.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Privy Treasurer Xu Zhenming and Censor Xu Dai proposed irrigated fields east of the capital; Lin strongly backed the plan, and it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 故事，戶部銀專供軍國，不給他用。

translations.literal: By precedent, Ministry of Revenue silver was exclusively for army and state, not supplied for other uses.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, Ministry of Revenue silver was reserved for military and state expenses and was not to be diverted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 帝大婚，暫取濟邊銀九萬兩為織造費，至是復欲行之，遴執爭。

translations.literal: When the emperor's grand wedding occurred, border-relief silver of ninety thousand taels was temporarily taken for weaving expenses; at this time they again wished to do this, and Lin firmly contested it.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's grand wedding, ninety thousand taels of frontier relief silver had been temporarily diverted for weaving costs; when the court tried again, Lin objected strenuously.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔取金四千兩為慈寧宮用，遴又力持。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict took four thousand taels of gold for use in the Cining Palace; Lin again firmly opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict ordered four thousand taels of gold for the Cining Palace, and Lin again resisted.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: All were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In each case his remonstrance was rejected.

sentences.zh: 已，陳理財七事，請崇節儉、重農務、督逋負、懲貪墨、廣儲蓄、飭貢市。

translations.literal: Thereafter, he set forth seven matters on managing finances, requesting honoring thrift, emphasizing agricultural affairs, supervising arrears, punishing corruption, broadening storage, and regulating tribute markets.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted seven proposals on fiscal management, calling for thrift, emphasis on agriculture, collection of arrears, punishment of graft, expanded reserves, and tighter regulation of tribute trade.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「事關朕躬者已知之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied saying: 'Matters concerning my own person I already know.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'As for matters touching me personally, I am already aware.

sentences.zh: 餘飭所司議行。」

translations.literal: The rest order the responsible offices to discuss and carry out."
translations.idiomatic: Let the rest be referred to the appropriate offices for deliberation and implementation."

sentences.zh: 時釋教大盛，遴請汰其壯者歸農，聚眾修齋者坐左道罪。

translations.literal: At that time Buddhism greatly flourished; Lin requested weeding out the strong among them to return to farming, and those gathering crowds to perform fasting rituals were charged with heterodox teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was then flourishing; Lin urged that able-bodied monks be sent back to farming and that those who assembled crowds for ritual observances be punished for heterodox practices.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書沈鯉請如遴言。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Shen Li requested to follow Lin's words.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Shen Li endorsed Lin's proposal.

sentences.zh: 詔已許，後妃宦官多言不便，事中止。

translations.literal: An edict had already assented, but consorts and eunuchs many spoke that it was inconvenient, and the affair stopped midway.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had been approved, but consorts and eunuchs protested that it would be impractical, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 遼東總兵官李成梁賂遺遍輦轂，不敢至遴門。

translations.literal: Liaodong regional commander Li Chengliang's bribes and gifts pervaded the capital, yet he did not dare come to Lin's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang, commander of Liaodong, bestowed bribes throughout the capital but would not venture near Lin's door.

sentences.zh: 遴在戶部頻執爭，已為中官所嫉。

translations.literal: Lin at the Ministry of Revenue frequently firmly contested; he had already been envied by eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated objections while at the Ministry of Revenue had already earned the enmity of the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 會帝閱壽宮，中官持禦批索馬。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor inspected the mausoleum; a eunuch held an imperial rescript demanding horses.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was inspecting his tomb site, a eunuch arrived with an imperial rescript demanding horses.

sentences.zh: 遴以為題本當鈐印，司禮傳奉由科發部，無徑下部者，援故事執奏。

translations.literal: Lin considered that memorial titles should bear seals; the Directorate of Ceremonial transmitted orders issued through the secretariat to the ministries—there was none sent directly to a ministry; citing precedent he memorialized and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued that sealed memorials should go through proper channels: the Directorate of Ceremonial relayed imperial orders via the secretariat to the ministries, and none should bypass that route; citing precedent, he refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行嘗以管事指揮羅秀屬遴補錦衣僉書，遴格不許。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing once asked the supervisory commander Luo Xiu to be entrusted to Lin to fill the post of Assistant Director in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; Lin rejected and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing once asked Lin to appoint the duty officer Luo Xiu as Assistant Director of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; Lin refused.

sentences.zh: 時行乃調旨責遴擅留禦批，失敬上體。

translations.literal: Shixing then adjusted the edict to rebuke Lin for presumptuously retaining the imperial rescript, failing to respect the emperor's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing then drafted an edict rebuking Lin for unlawfully withholding the imperial rescript and showing disrespect to the throne.

sentences.zh: 御史因交章劾遴，遴乞休去，張佳胤代之。

translations.literal: Censors thereupon submitted memorials one after another impeaching Lin; Lin begged to retire and leave, and Zhang Jiayin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then launched a concerted impeachment; Lin requested retirement and was replaced by Zhang Jiayin.

sentences.zh: 給事中張養蒙言：「羅秀本太監滕祥奴，賄入禁衛。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yangmeng said: 'Luo Xiu was originally the slave of eunuch Teng Xiang; by bribe he entered the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yangmeng said: 'Luo Xiu was originally a bondservant of the eunuch Teng Xiang and bought his way into the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 往歲營僉書，尚書遴持正，為所中傷去。

translations.literal: In past years when seeking the assistant director post, Minister Lin held upright and was slandered by them and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the assistant directorship came open last year, Minister Lin stood firm and was driven out by their slander.

sentences.zh: 未幾秀即躐用，物議沸騰。」

translations.literal: Before long Xiu was immediately promoted out of turn, and public opinion seethed."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luo was promoted ahead of his rank, and public outrage erupted."

sentences.zh: 於是黜秀，佳胤亦罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiu was dismissed, and Jiayin was also removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was then dismissed, and Jiayin was removed as well.

sentences.zh: 遴雖退，聲望愈重，以年高存問者再三。

translations.literal: Although Lin retired, his reputation grew heavier; because of advanced age, inquiries were sent again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lin had left office, his standing only grew; the court repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after him in his old age.

sentences.zh: 三十六年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-sixth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，追謚恭肅。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period, posthumously he was given the posthumous title Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was posthumously honored with the epithet Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 畢鏘，字廷鳴，石埭人。

translations.literal: Bi Qiang, courtesy name Tingming, was a man of Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Qiang, styled Tingming, was from Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，擢浙江提學副使，遷廣西右參政，進按察使，再遷湖廣左布政使。

translations.literal: He passed through director rank, was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Education of Zhejiang, transferred to Right Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, advanced to Surveillance Commissioner, and again transferred to Left Provincial Administrator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a director, he was promoted Vice Commissioner of Education for Zhejiang, transferred to Right Vice Commissioner in Guangxi, raised to Surveillance Commissioner, and then moved to Left Provincial Administrator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 召為太仆卿，未至，改應天尹。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Court of the Imperial Stud minister; before arriving, he was changed to Governor of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Stud, but before taking up the post was reassigned Governor of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 海瑞撫江南，移檄京府，等於屬吏，鏘卻不受。

translations.literal: Hai Rui governed Jiangnan and sent a dispatch to the capital prefecture, treating it as a subordinate official; Qiang refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Hai Rui governed Jiangnan he issued orders to the capital prefecture as though it were subordinate to him; Bi Qiang refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 瑞察鏘政，更與善。

translations.literal: Rui observed Qiang's governance and came to be on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Rui observed Bi's administration and came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 進南京戶部右侍郎，督理糧儲。

translations.literal: He advanced to Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, supervising grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, with charge of granary affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，入為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 改戶部，總督倉場。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Ministry of Revenue, supervising the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue as Supervisor of the Granaries.

sentences.zh: 擢南京戶部尚書，謝病去。

translations.literal: He was promoted Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Nanjing Minister of Revenue, he retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 起南京工部尚書，就改吏部，征為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was raised as Nanjing Minister of Works, immediately changed to the Ministry of Personnel, and summoned as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Nanjing Minister of Works, he was promptly transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and then summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝以風霾諭所司陳時政，鏘以九事上。

translations.literal: Because of wind and haze the emperor ordered responsible offices to set forth current policies; Qiang submitted nine matters.
translations.idiomatic: When sandstorms prompted the emperor to call for comments on current policy, Bi submitted nine recommendations.

sentences.zh: 中言：「錦衣旗校至萬七千四百余人，內府諸監局匠役數亦稱是。

translations.literal: Among them he said: 'Embroidered Uniform Guard banner officers and scouts reach more than seventeen thousand four hundred persons; the inner palace's various directorates' craftsmen and laborers are likewise in number.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, in part: 'Embroidered Uniform Guard agents number more than 17,400, and the inner palace workshops employ just as many.

sentences.zh: 此冗食之尤，宜屏除冒濫。

translations.literal: This is the extreme of redundant eaters; one should purge false and excessive ones.
translations.idiomatic: These are the worst of idle mouths on the state payroll; spurious and excessive posts should be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 州縣丈田滋弊，雲南鼓鑄不酬工直，官已裁而復置，田欲墾而再停。

translations.literal: At district and county level land survey proliferates abuses; Yunnan coin casting does not repay workers' wages; offices already cut were restored; fields sought to be reclaimed were again halted.
translations.idiomatic: Land surveys at the county level breed corruption; Yunnan minting fails to pay fair wages; posts abolished are reinstated, and land reclamation projects are halted just as they begin.

sentences.zh: 請酌土俗人情，毋率意更改。

translations.literal: He requested weighing local custom and human sentiment, not arbitrarily altering.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that local customs be respected and that policy not be changed recklessly.

sentences.zh: 至袍服錦綺，歲有積余，何煩頻織。

translations.literal: As for robes, clothing, brocade and gauze, each year there are accumulated surpluses—why trouble frequent weaving?
translations.idiomatic: Robes and brocades already accumulate surplus year after year—why keep weaving more?

sentences.zh: 天燈費巨萬，尤不經。

translations.literal: Sky-lamp expenses reach tens of thousands—especially improper.
translations.idiomatic: The cost of sky lanterns runs to tens of thousands of taels—a particularly wasteful extravagance.

sentences.zh: 濫予不可不裁，淫巧不可不革。」

translations.literal: Indiscriminate grants must be cut; extravagant craft must be reformed."
translations.idiomatic: Indiscriminate spending must be curtailed and frivolous luxuries abolished."

sentences.zh: 他所奏，並多切要。

translations.literal: His other memorialized items were also many and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: His other proposals were likewise sharp and to the point.

sentences.zh: 近幸從中撓之，不盡行。

translations.literal: Favored intimates from within obstructed them; not all were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites at court intervened to block them, and most were never implemented.

sentences.zh: 鏘乃引年乞罷。

translations.literal: Qiang thereupon cited age and begged to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then cited his age and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 予馳驛歸。

translations.literal: He was granted post-horses and returned by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted relay horses for the journey home.

sentences.zh: 鏘遇事守正，有物望。

translations.literal: Qiang in handling affairs upheld rectitude and had public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was known for integrity and commanded wide respect.

sentences.zh: 年及八十，賜存問，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When his age reached eighty, he was granted an inquiry visit and given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When he turned eighty, the throne sent envoys to inquire after him and conferred on him the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後凡存問者再。

translations.literal: Later, inquiries in all occurred twice more.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent further inquiries twice thereafter.

sentences.zh: 其孫汝楩奉表入謝，詔以為太學生。

translations.literal: His grandson Ru Man presented a memorial entering to give thanks; an edict made him an Imperial Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandson Ru Man came to court with a memorial of thanks, the emperor enrolled him as a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 年九十三而卒。

translations.literal: At age ninety-three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚恭介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and posthumous title Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the epithet Gongjie.

sentences.zh: 舒化，字汝德，臨川人。

translations.literal: Shu Hua, courtesy name Rude, was a man of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua, styled Rude, was from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授衡州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate-investigator of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 改補鳳陽，擢戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to fill Fengyang, promoted to supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fengyang, he was promoted supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，三遷刑科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, through three promotions he became supervising secretary of the Justice Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he rose through three promotions to supervising secretary in the Justice Section.

sentences.zh: 帝任宦官，旨多從中下。

translations.literal: The emperor relied on eunuchs; edicts mostly issued from below within.
