translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted power to eunuchs, and edicts often issued from behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 化言：「法者天下之公，大小罪犯宜悉付法司。

translations.literal: Hua said: 'Law is the public thing of the empire; crimes great and small should all be entrusted to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued: 'The law belongs to the realm as a whole; crimes great and small ought to be handed entirely to the judicial bureaus.

sentences.zh: 不當，則臣等論劾。

translations.literal: If not proper, then we ministers debate and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: If their rulings are wrong, we ministers may impeach them.

sentences.zh: 若竟自敕行，則喜怒未必當，而法司與臣等俱虛設。」

translations.literal: If in the end edicts are issued directly, then joy and anger may not be appropriate, and the judicial offices together with us ministers are all set up in vain."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne instead issues edicts directly, judgments may reflect mere caprice, and both the judicial offices and we censors become figureheads."

sentences.zh: 詔是其言。

translations.literal: An edict approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: An edict endorsed his view.

sentences.zh: 冬至郊天，聞帝咳聲，推論陰陽後復之漸，請法天養微陽，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice sacrifice to Heaven, hearing the emperor's cough, he inferred the gradual restoration of yin and yang afterward, and requested following Heaven to nurture slight yang; his words were very earnest and direct.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice sacrifice to Heaven he heard the emperor cough, interpreted it as a sign that yin was overpowering yang, and urged him to heed Heaven and nurture his vital yang—the memorial was blunt and urgent.

sentences.zh: 有詔言災眚洊至，由部院政事不修，令廠衛密察。

translations.literal: There was an edict saying calamities and portents arrived repeatedly, because ministries and courts did not cultivate affairs; it ordered the factories and guards to secretly investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict blamed recurring disasters on negligence in the ministries and ordered the secret police to conduct covert surveillance.

sentences.zh: 化偕同列言：「廠衛僥巡輦下，惟詰奸宄、禁盜賊耳。

translations.literal: Hua together with his colleagues said: 'The factories and guards patrol under the imperial carriage only to examine traitors and villains and forbid thieves and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and his colleagues responded: 'The secret police patrol the capital only to hunt traitors and suppress bandits.

sentences.zh: 駕馭百官，乃天子權，而糾察非法，則責在臺諫，豈廠衛所得幹。

translations.literal: Driving and controlling the hundred officials is the Son of Heaven's power, while investigating and correcting unlawful conduct is the responsibility of the censorate and remonstrators—how can the factories and guards be permitted to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the bureaucracy is the emperor's prerogative, and policing official misconduct falls to the censorate—what business is that of the secret police?

sentences.zh: 今命之刺訪，將必開羅織之門，逞機阱之術，禍貽善類，使人人重足累息，何以為治。

translations.literal: Now ordering them to spy and investigate will necessarily open the gate of fabrication, display the art of entrapment, bring calamity upon good people, and make every man tread heavily and breathe in fear—how can there be governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering them to gather intelligence will open the door to manufactured charges and entrapment, harm the innocent, and leave everyone walking on eggshells—how is that governance?

sentences.zh: 且廠衛非能自廉察，必屬之番校。

translations.literal: Moreover, the factories and guards cannot themselves inspect with integrity—they must assign to the runner scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the secret police cannot investigate honestly themselves; they must rely on their runner-agents.

sentences.zh: 陛下不信大臣，反信若屬耶？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not trust great ministers, yet trusts these sorts?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty trusts such men rather than your senior ministers?"

sentences.zh: 御史劉思賢等亦極陳其害。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Sixian and others also extremely set forth its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Sixian and others also spoke forcefully against the plan.

sentences.zh: 帝並不從。

translations.literal: The emperor altogether did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected them all.

sentences.zh: 已而事竟寢。

translations.literal: Before long the affair in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the matter was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 校尉負屍出北安門，兵馬指揮孫承芳見之，疑有奸，系獄鞫訊，詞連內官李陽春。

translations.literal: A runner guard carried a corpse out the North Peace Gate; Commander of the Capital Garrison Sun Chengfang saw it, suspected treachery, imprisoned and interrogated; testimony implicated inner eunuch Li Yangchun.
translations.idiomatic: A guard was seen carrying a corpse out through the North Peace Gate; Capital Garrison Commander Sun Chengfang, suspecting foul play, had him arrested and interrogated, and testimony implicated the eunuch Li Yangchun.

sentences.zh: 陽春懼，訴於帝。

translations.literal: Yangchun was afraid and appealed to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing arrest, Li Yangchun appealed directly to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 言尉所負非死者，出外乃死，承芳妄生事，刑校尉。

translations.literal: He said the guard had not carried the deceased—the man died only after going outside; Chengfang falsely created an incident and punished the runner guard.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the guard had been carrying a living man who died only after leaving the gate, that Sun Chengfang had manufactured the case, and that the runner guard had been wrongly punished.

sentences.zh: 帝信之，杖承芳六十，斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it, caned Chengfang sixty blows, and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, had Sun Chengfang beaten sixty strokes with the rod, and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 化請以陽春所奏下法司勘問，不納。

translations.literal: Hua requested that Yangchun's report be sent down to the judicial offices for investigation; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua asked that Yangchun's account be referred to the regular courts for review, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 四年熱審，請釋累臣鄭履淳、李芳，及朝審，又請釋李已，皆得宥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the hot-weather review, he requested release of long-imprisoned officials Zheng Luchun and Li Fang; at the court review as well he again requested release of Li Yi—all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer judicial review in his fourth year in office he secured the release of long-held prisoners Zheng Luchun and Li Fang; at the autumn court review he won pardon for Li Yi as well.

sentences.zh: 時高拱當國，路楷、楊順以構殺沈煉論死。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Gong held power; Lu Kai and Yang Shun were sentenced to death for framing and murdering Shen Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong was then dominant at court, and Lu Kai and Yang Shun had been condemned to death for framing and killing Shen Lian.

sentences.zh: 拱欲為楷地，謂順首禍，順死，楷可勿坐。

translations.literal: Gong wished to make room for Kai, saying Shun was the primary culprit—if Shun died, Kai need not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong wanted to spare Lu Kai, arguing that Yang Shun had been the ringleader and that Kai should go unpunished once Shun was executed.

sentences.zh: 化取獄牘示拱曰：「獄故無煉名。

translations.literal: Hua took the prison records and showed Gong, saying: "The records originally have no name of Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua produced the case file and showed it to Gao Gong, saying, "Shen Lian's name does not appear in the original records at all.

sentences.zh: 有之，自楷始。

translations.literal: If there is one, it begins with Kai.
translations.idiomatic: If a name does appear, Lu Kai's is the first.

sentences.zh: 楷誠罪首。」

translations.literal: Kai is truly the chief criminal."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai is plainly the principal offender."

sentences.zh: 拱又議宥方士王金等罪，化言：「此遺詔意，即欲勿罪，宜何辭？」

translations.literal: Gong again discussed pardoning the fangshi Wang Jin and others' crimes. Hua said: "This was the late emperor's will—even if you wish not to punish, what wording should be used?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong then proposed pardoning the immortal masters Wang Jin and others. Shu Hua objected: "The late emperor's dying wish was to spare them—but if you mean to pardon them now, what language can justify it?"

sentences.zh: 忤拱，出為陜西參政。

translations.literal: Offending Gong, he was sent out as Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Having crossed Gao Gong, he was transferred out to serve as vice commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 再疏致仕歸。

translations.literal: Again memorialized to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial requesting retirement and went home.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，累擢太僕少卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he rose through several posts to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 復以疾歸。

translations.literal: Again returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness soon forced him to retire once more.

sentences.zh: 由南京大理卿召拜刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: From Grand Court of Revision at Nanjing, he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from the Nanjing Court of Revision and appointed Left Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 雲南緬賊平，帝御午門樓受俘。

translations.literal: When Yunnan Burmese rebels were pacified, the emperor attended the Meridian Gate tower to receive captives.
translations.idiomatic: After the Burmese rebels in Yunnan were subdued, the emperor took the captives in state at the Meridian Gate tower.

sentences.zh: 化讀奏詞，音吐洪亮，進止有儀，帝目屬之。

translations.literal: Hua read the memorial wording; his voice was resonant, his bearing measured—the emperor's eyes fixed on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu Hua read the memorial aloud, his voice rang clear and his deportment was dignified; the emperor's eyes never left him.

sentences.zh: 會刑部缺尚書，手詔用化。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Justice lacked a minister, the emperor personally issued an edict to use Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Ministry of Justice fell vacant, and the emperor personally appointed Shu Hua minister.

sentences.zh: 化言：「陛下仁心出天性。

translations.literal: Hua said: "Your Majesty's benevolent heart springs from innate nature.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua said, "Your Majesty's mercy is rooted in your nature.

sentences.zh: 知府錢若賡、知州方復乾以殘酷死戍。

translations.literal: Prefect Qian Ruogeng and Prefect Fang Fuqian died on penal frontier service because of cruel sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Prefect Qian Ruogeng and Prefect Fang Fuqian were sent to die on the frontier after sentences far harsher than the law allowed.

sentences.zh: 請飭大小臣僚各遵律例，毋淫刑。

translations.literal: I request instructing ministers and officials of all ranks each to follow statutes and not apply excessive punishments.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to instruct every official, high and low, to abide by the code and cease imposing punishments beyond the law.

sentences.zh: 《大明律》一書，高皇帝揭之兩廡，手加更定。

translations.literal: The book Great Ming Code—the Supreme Emperor displayed it in both galleries and personally revised and fixed it.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor himself revised the Great Ming Code and had it posted in both wings of the palace.

sentences.zh: 今未經詳斷者或命從重擬議，已經定議者又詔加等處斬，是謂律不足用也。

translations.literal: Now cases not yet fully judged are sometimes ordered to be deliberated with heavier penalties; cases already decided are again issued an edict for escalated execution—this means the code is deemed insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Today open cases are often ordered retried under heavier penalties, and settled ones are suddenly escalated to execution by imperial edict—as though the code itself were no longer adequate.

sentences.zh: 去冬雨雪不時，災異頻見，咎當在此。」

translations.literal: Last winter snow and rain came untimely; calamities and portents appeared frequently—the blame should lie here."
translations.idiomatic: Last winter's untimely snow and rain and the portents that have followed surely stem from this."

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a warm and approving edict.

sentences.zh: 會續修《會典》，因輯嘉靖三十四年以後事例與刑名相關者三百八十二條，奏之。

translations.literal: When the Collected Statutes were being revised, he compiled 382 precedents related to criminal matters from after the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: While the Collected Statutes were being revised, he gathered 382 criminal precedents dating from the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing onward and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔頒示中外。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them promulgated within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their publication throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 十四年，應詔陳言。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, in response to an edict soliciting opinions, he presented memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he answered an imperial call for candid advice with a series of memorials.

sentences.zh: 請信詔令，清獄訟，速訊讞，嚴檢驗，禁冤濫，而以格天安民歸本聖心。

translations.literal: He requested trusting edicts, clearing prisons and lawsuits, speeding trial and judgment, strict forensic examination, forbidding wrongful conviction and abuse—and returning the foundation of matching Heaven and settling the people to the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to honor his own edicts, clear the prisons, expedite trials, tighten forensic standards, and stop wrongful convictions—so that harmonizing Heaven and securing the people would again rest on the throne's own conscience.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice and took it to heart.

sentences.zh: 帝慮群下欺罔，間有訐發，輒遣官逮捕，牽引證佐，文案累積。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that officials deceived him; whenever there were denunciations, he immediately sent officers to arrest, dragging in witnesses, documents piling up.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing deception among his officials, the emperor would dispatch arresting officers at the slightest accusation, sweeping up witnesses and witnesses' witnesses until the paperwork piled high.

sentences.zh: 化言：「主術貴執要，不當侵有司；

translations.literal: Hua said: "The ruler's art values grasping essentials; one should not encroach on the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua argued: "The art of rule lies in holding to essentials; the throne should not usurp the duties of the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 徒使人歸過於上，而下得緣以飾非。」

translations.literal: It merely makes people assign blame to the ruler above, while those below can use the occasion to cover faults."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise blame falls upward while subordinates seize the chance to conceal their own misconduct."

sentences.zh: 潞王府小校以事為兵馬司吏目所笞，帝怒，逮吏目下詔獄，掠死，又罪其捕卒七人。

translations.literal: A minor officer of the Prince of Lu's establishment was caned by a clerk of the Capital Garrison for some matter; the emperor was angry, had the clerk seized to the imperial prison where he died under torture, and also blamed seven arresting guards.
translations.idiomatic: When a minor retainer of the Prince of Lu was beaten by a Capital Garrison clerk, the emperor flew into a rage, had the clerk thrown into the imperial prison—where he died under torture—and punished seven guards who had helped make the arrest.

sentences.zh: 化爭之。

translations.literal: Hua disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua protested vigorously.

sentences.zh: 詔罪為首一人，余並獲宥。

translations.literal: An edict punished only the chief culprit; the rest all received pardon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict finally punished only the ringleader and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 明年，京察拾遺，南京科道論及化。

translations.literal: The next year, during the capital evaluation's supplemental review, Nanjing censors and remonstrators discussed Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, during the supplemental round of the capital personnel review, Nanjing censors and remonstrators raised complaints against him.

sentences.zh: 遂三疏乞歸。

translations.literal: He then submitted three memorials begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He responded with three successive memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 會當慮囚，復起視事。

translations.literal: When it came time for reviewing prisoners, he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: When the annual prison review came due, he returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 中貴傳帝意宥重辟三十余人，化爭不可。

translations.literal: A eunuch transmitted the emperor's wish to pardon thirty-odd men facing severe punishment; Hua argued it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch conveyed the emperor's wish to pardon more than thirty men facing capital sentences; Shu Hua insisted it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 詔卒從其議。

translations.literal: An edict in the end followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ultimately sided with him.

sentences.zh: 尋稱病篤，乃聽歸。

translations.literal: Soon claiming serious illness, he was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, pleading grave illness, he was at last permitted to go home.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，謚莊僖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and posthumous title Zhuangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the epithet Zhuangxi.

sentences.zh: 李世達，字子成，涇陽人。

translations.literal: Li Shida, courtesy name Zicheng, was a man of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shida, styled Zicheng, was from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，歷考功、文選郎中，與陸光祖並為尚書所倚。

translations.literal: He transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, served as director in the Performance Evaluation and Selection bureaus, and with Lu Guangzu was equally relied on by the minister.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he served as director in the Performance Evaluation and Selection bureaus and, together with Lu Guangzu, became one of the minister's most trusted men.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，丁曾祖憂。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing, he entered mourning for his great-grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he withdrew to mourn his great-grandfather.

sentences.zh: 起右通政，歷南京太仆卿。

translations.literal: Recalled as Right Vice Commissioner for Transmission, he served as Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Right Vice Commissioner for Transmission, he later held the post of Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年以右僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he governed Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 尋進右副都御史，總理河道。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and supervised river channels.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief with charge of the waterways.

sentences.zh: 未上，改撫浙江。

translations.literal: Before taking office, he was changed to governing Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume that post, he was reassigned to govern Zhejiang instead.

sentences.zh: 旋移疾歸，起督漕運兼巡撫鳳陽。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and returned; recalled to supervise grain transport and govern Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on grounds of illness, but was recalled to supervise the grain transport and serve as grand coordinator of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 黃河南侵，淮安告警，世達請修石堤捍城；

translations.literal: The Yellow River encroached south; Huai'an raised alarms; Shida requested building stone dikes to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River shifted south and Huai'an came under threat, Shida proposed building stone embankments to shield the city.

sentences.zh: 寶應氾光湖風濤險惡，歲漂溺，請開越河殺水勢。

translations.literal: Baoying's Fan'guang Lake had fierce winds and waves and yearly flooding; he requested opening a bypass river to reduce the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: At Baoying, where Fan'guang Lake's storms caused annual flooding, he asked permission to cut a diversion channel to bleed off the floodwaters.

sentences.zh: 俱報可。

translations.literal: Both were reported approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His next appointment was Right Vice Minister of War at the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 召改戶部，復改吏部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Recalled, changed to the Ministry of Revenue, then again to Personnel, and advanced to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was moved first to the Ministry of Revenue and then to Personnel, rising to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 擢南京吏部尚書，就改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Promoted to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, immediately changed to War, assisting confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, he was immediately shifted to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 中官張德毆人死，世達請置於理，刑科唐堯欽亦言之，德遂屬吏。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang De beat a man to death; Shida requested placing him before the law; Tang Yaoqin of the Punishments Section also spoke; De was then entrusted to officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Zhang De beat a man to death, Shida demanded that he be handed over for trial; Tang Yaoqin of the Punishments Section backed him, and Zhang De was turned over to the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 大興知縣王階坐撻樂舞生下吏，帝密遣兩校尉偵之，讞日為巡風主事孫承榮所拒。

translations.literal: The Daxing magistrate Wang Jie was demoted for beating music students; the emperor secretly sent two runner guards to spy; on judgment day he was rejected by Touring Inspection Director Sun Chengrong.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wang Jie of Daxing was demoted for beating court musicians; the emperor secretly sent two runner guards to monitor the trial, but on judgment day Sun Chengrong, director of touring inspection, turned them away.

sentences.zh: 校尉還奏，帝怒詰世達。

translations.literal: The runner guards returned and reported; the emperor angrily interrogated Shida.
translations.idiomatic: When the runners reported back, the emperor angrily summoned Shida for an explanation.

sentences.zh: 世達言偵伺非大體。

translations.literal: Shida said covert surveillance is not the great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Shida replied that covert surveillance was no way to run a court.

sentences.zh: 承榮竟奪俸。

translations.literal: Chengrong in the end had his salary stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chengrong, however, was stripped of his salary.

sentences.zh: 東廠太監張鯨有罪，言官交劾，帝曲貸之。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot director Zhang Jin had guilt; censorial officials jointly impeached him; the emperor bent to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Depot eunuch Zhang Jin was found guilty and impeached by a chorus of censors, the emperor bent the rules to protect him.

sentences.zh: 世達執奏，帝乃屏鯨於外。

translations.literal: Shida submitted firmly; the emperor then barred Jin outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shida pressed his case in memorial after memorial until the emperor finally banished Zhang Jin from court.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉侯拱宸仆斃平民抵法，世達請並坐拱宸。

translations.literal: Commandant-in-Chief Hou Gongchen's servant killed a commoner and faced the law; Shida requested joint punishment of Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's son-in-law Hou Gongchen's servant killed a commoner and stood trial, Shida asked that Gongchen be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 乃革其任，命國學肄禮。

translations.literal: The emperor then stripped his appointment and ordered him to study rites at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped him of his post and ordered him to study ritual at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 罪人焦文粲法不當死，帝怒入之。

translations.literal: The criminal Jiao Wencan by law should not die; the emperor angrily had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The convict Jiao Wencan did not deserve death under the code, but the emperor in anger had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會朝審，命戶部尚書宋纁主筆。

translations.literal: At the court review, the emperor ordered Revenue Minister Song Li to lead the drafting.
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn court review the emperor ordered Revenue Minister Song Li to draft the sentence.

sentences.zh: 世達言於纁，薄文粲罪。

translations.literal: Shida spoke to Li and lightened Wencan's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shida persuaded Song Li to reduce the charge against Jiao Wencan.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，詰問，復據法以對。

translations.literal: Offending the imperial will, he was interrogated and again answered according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Called before the emperor for defying his wishes, he answered every question by citing the law.

sentences.zh: 帝卒不從。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not yield.

sentences.zh: 時帝燕居多暴怒，近侍屢以非罪死，世達因災異上書以諷。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor in leisure often flew into violent anger; close attendants repeatedly died for no crime; Shida because of calamities and portents memorialized to admonish indirectly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then given to sudden rages in private, and attendants were often executed on trivial grounds; Shida seized on recent portents to submit a veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 浙江饑，或請令罪人出粟除罪。

translations.literal: Zhejiang suffered famine; some requested letting criminals contribute grain to remove guilt.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Zhejiang, some officials proposed letting convicts buy their freedom with grain.

sentences.zh: 世達言：「法不可廢，寧赦毋贖。

translations.literal: Shida said: "The law cannot be abolished; better pardon than redeem.
translations.idiomatic: Shida objected: "The law must not be set aside; it is better to grant pardon than to accept ransom.

sentences.zh: 赦則恩出於上，法猶存。

translations.literal: With pardon, grace comes from above and the law still exists.
translations.idiomatic: A pardon keeps mercy in the emperor's hands and leaves the law intact.

sentences.zh: 贖則力出於下，人滋玩。」

translations.literal: With redemption, power comes from below and people increasingly treat the law lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Ransom puts power in the hands of the wealthy and teaches everyone to treat punishment as a price."

sentences.zh: 識者韙之。

translations.literal: The knowing praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment applauded the argument.

sentences.zh: 改左都御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 兵馬指揮何價虐死三人，御史劉思瑜庇之。

translations.literal: Capital Garrison Commander He Jia tortured three men to death; Censor Liu Siyu sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Garrison Commander He Jia had tortured three men to death, and Censor Liu Siyu shielded him from prosecution.

sentences.zh: 世達劾奏，帝鐫思瑜秩。

translations.literal: Shida impeached and memorialized; the emperor cut Siyu's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shida impeached them both, and the emperor demoted Liu Siyu.

sentences.zh: 復劾罷御史韓介等數人。

translations.literal: Again he impeached and dismissed several men including Censor Han Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to impeach and dismiss several other censors, including Han Jie.

sentences.zh: 帝深惡言官，下詔申飭，責以挾私報復。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply hated remonstrating officials, issued an edict admonishing them, and blamed them for using private motives to retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply resentful of the censorate, the emperor issued an edict rebuking remonstrators for pursuing private vendettas.

sentences.zh: 世達言：「效忠持正者，語雖過激，心實無他。

translations.literal: Shida said: "Those loyal and upright—though their words be excessive, their hearts truly have no other motive.
translations.idiomatic: Shida replied: "Men who serve loyally and speak plainly may sound harsh, but their hearts are clean.

sentences.zh: 即或心未可知，而言不可廢，並宜容納。

translations.literal: Even if the heart cannot be known, words cannot be discarded—all should be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Even when motives are unclear, their words must still be heard and tolerated.

sentences.zh: 惟緘默依阿，然後加黜罰。

translations.literal: Only for silence and sycophancy should dismissal and punishment be added.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment should fall only on those who keep silent and flatter.

sentences.zh: 則讜言日進，邪說漸消。」

translations.literal: Then forthright speech will daily advance and evil talk gradually vanish."
translations.idiomatic: Then honest counsel will flow daily and corrupt counsel will fade."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: A reply noted receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The throne acknowledged the memorial.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，與吏部尚書孫鑨同主京察，斥政府私人殆盡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, with Personnel Minister Sun Luang he jointly chaired the capital evaluation and dismissed the government's private favorites nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he and Personnel Minister Sun Luang presided over the capital evaluation and cleared out nearly every protégé of the ruling faction.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中趙南星被劾貶官，世達力爭之，反除南星等名，遂求去，不許。

translations.literal: Performance Evaluation Director Zhao Nanxing was impeached and demoted; Shida forcefully argued against it, but conversely Nanxing and others were removed from their names; he then sought to leave and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Performance Evaluation Director Zhao Nanxing was impeached and demoted, Shida fought hard for him—but Nanxing and his allies were dismissed instead; Shida then asked to retire and was refused.

sentences.zh: 其秋，吏部侍郎趙用賢以絕婚事被訐，世達白其無罪。

translations.literal: That autumn, Personnel Vice Minister Zhao Yongxian was denounced over breaking off a marriage; Shida declared him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Vice Minister Zhao Yongxian was accused over a broken marriage engagement, Shida testified to his innocence.

sentences.zh: 郎中楊應宿、鄭材疏詆世達，遂連章乞休去。

translations.literal: Directors Yang Yingsu and Zheng Cai memorialized slandering Shida; he then submitted linked memorials begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Directors Yang Yingsu and Zheng Cai then memorialized against him; Shida responded with a string of retirement petitions.

sentences.zh: 歸七年卒。

translations.literal: He returned home; seven years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and died seven years later.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚敏肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and posthumous title Minsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the epithet Minsu.

sentences.zh: 曾同亨，字於野，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zeng Tongheng, courtesy name Yuye, was a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Tongheng, styled Yuye, was from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 父存仁，雲南布政使。

translations.literal: His father Cunren was Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunren had served as administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 同亨舉嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: Tongheng passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1559, Tongheng became a jinshi graduate.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He received a post as principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 改禮部，遷吏部文選主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and then promoted to principal secretary for literary selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a move to the Ministry of Rites, he was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel's office for literary selection.

sentences.zh: 故事，丞簿以下官，聽胥吏銓註，同亨悉躬親之。

translations.literal: By precedent, appointments for officials below assistant commissioner and registrar rank were left to clerks to assign; Tongheng personally handled all of them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Established practice had allowed clerks to fill posts below the rank of assistant commissioner, but Tongheng took personal charge of every such appointment.

sentences.zh: 與陸光祖、李世達齊名。

translations.literal: He was renowned alongside Lu Guangzu and Li Shida.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation matched that of Lu Guangzu and Li Shida.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，為文選郎中，薦用遺佚幾盡。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing, as director of literary selection, he recommended and employed nearly all overlooked and neglected talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign, as director of literary selection, he brought back into service nearly every worthy official who had been passed over.

sentences.zh: 進太常少卿，請急去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and urgently requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he begged permission to resign at once.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，起大理少卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli, he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli reign began, he was summoned back as vice minister of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 歷順天府尹，以右副都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: He served successively as Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and then as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as prefect of Shuntian and then as right vice censor-in-chief and governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 御史劉臺得罪張居正，同亨，臺姊夫也，給事中陳三謨欲並逐之，奏同亨羸不任職。

translations.literal: The Censor Liu Tai offended Zhang Juzheng; Tongheng was Tai's brother-in-law. The Supervising Secretary Chen Sanmo wished to remove both and memorialized that Tongheng was weak and unfit for office.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor Liu Tai fell afoul of Zhang Juzheng, the supervising secretary Chen Sanmo tried to purge Tongheng too—Tai's brother-in-law—claiming in a memorial that Tongheng was too frail to hold his post.

sentences.zh: 詔調南京，遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: An edict transferred him to Nanjing, whereupon he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered transferred to Nanjing but instead cited illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 九年，京察拾遺，給事中奏燿、御史錢岱等復希居正指，列同亨名。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, during the capital evaluation of surplus officials, the Supervising Secretaries Qin Yao and Censor Qian Dai and others again followed Zhang Juzheng's wishes and listed Tongheng's name.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 9, during the capital review of surplus officials, the supervising secretaries Qin Yao and the censor Qian Dai once more did Zhang Juzheng's bidding and put Tongheng on the list.

sentences.zh: 勒休致。

translations.literal: He was compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，起南京太常卿。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, Tongheng was recalled as Minister of Ceremonies at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Juzheng died, he was recalled as minister of imperial sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召為大理卿，遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Minister of Revision and promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to head the Court of Revision, he was then made right vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 督治壽宮，節浮費三十余萬。

translations.literal: He supervised construction of the imperial tomb and trimmed superfluous expenses by more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Overseeing construction of the imperial tomb, he cut wasteful spending by over three hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 由左侍郎進尚書。

translations.literal: From Left Vice Minister he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from left vice minister to full minister.

sentences.zh: 軍器自外輸，率不中程，奏請半收其直，又請減織造之半。

translations.literal: Military equipment supplied from outside generally failed to meet specifications; he memorialized to accept only half payment and also requested halving textile manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Arms shipped in from the provinces usually fell short of standard; he proposed paying only half price for substandard goods and cutting textile production in half.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 汝安王妃乞橋稅，同亨拒之。

translations.literal: The Princess Consort of Prince Ru'an requested bridge tolls; Tongheng refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess consort of the Prince of Ru'an asked for bridge toll revenue, Tongheng turned her down.

sentences.zh: 帝竟如妃請。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately granted the princess consort's request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with the princess consort in the end.

sentences.zh: 內府工匠，隆慶初數至萬五千八百人，尋汰二千五百人，而中官濫增不已。

translations.literal: Palace artisans numbered as many as fifteen thousand eight hundred at the start of Longqing; soon two thousand five hundred were cut, but eunuch officials continued to add posts recklessly without end.
translations.idiomatic: Palace workshops had swelled to 15,800 artisans at the start of Longqing; though 2,500 were soon dismissed, eunuchs kept inflating the rolls without restraint.

sentences.zh: 同亨疏請清厘。

translations.literal: Tongheng memorialized requesting a thorough purge and review.
translations.idiomatic: Tongheng submitted a memorial calling for a full audit.

sentences.zh: 已得旨，中官復奏寢之。

translations.literal: Having already received imperial approval, eunuch officials again memorialized and shelved it.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the emperor had given his assent, palace eunuchs blocked the order.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊其休疏爭，弗納。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Yang Qixiu memorialized in protest; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Yang Qixiu protested in a memorial, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 同亨弟乾亨請裁冗員以裕經費，京衛諸武臣謂減己月俸也，大嘩，伺同亨出朝，圍而噪之。

translations.literal: Tongheng's younger brother Qianheng requested cutting redundant posts to ease expenses; the military officers of the capital garrisons took this to mean reducing their monthly salaries and made a great uproar, waiting until Tongheng left court to surround and jeer at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongheng's brother Qianheng proposed trimming redundant posts to save funds, capital garrison officers—fearing cuts to their pay—raised such a clamor that they waited outside court and mobbed Tongheng on his way out.

sentences.zh: 同亨再乞休，不得請。

translations.literal: Tongheng again begged to retire but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tongheng asked again to resign, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 九門工成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When work on the Nine Gates was completed, he was granted the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion of the Nine Gates project, he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 力乞去，詔乘傳歸。

translations.literal: He strenuously begged to leave; an edict ordered him to return home by imperial post-horses.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for release, and the emperor granted him leave to return home with official transport.

sentences.zh: 起南京吏部尚書，辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing and declined the appointment without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as minister of personnel at Nanjing, he refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，再起故官，累辭乃就職。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again recalled to his former office; having declined repeatedly, he finally took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was summoned back to the same post; only after many refusals did he accept.

sentences.zh: 稅使所在虐民，同亨極諫。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners everywhere oppressed the people; Tongheng memorialized strenuously in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever tax agents went they abused the people, and Tongheng remonstrated forcefully against it.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，大計京官，與考功郎徐必達持正不撓。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, during the grand evaluation of capital officials, he and the Evaluation Director Xu Bidaa held firm and unbending to what was right.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 33, during the grand evaluation of capital officials, he and Xu Bidaa, director of evaluations, stood their ground without yielding.

sentences.zh: 是年，北察失執政意，中旨留給事中錢夢臯等；

translations.literal: That year the northern evaluation displeased the chief ministers; an edict from the inner court retained the Supervising Secretaries Qian Menggao and others;
translations.idiomatic: That year the northern evaluation ran counter to the chief ministers' wishes, and an edict from the inner court kept supervising secretaries such as Qian Menggao on the rolls;

sentences.zh: 南察及同亨自陳疏，亦久不下。

translations.literal: the southern evaluation and Tongheng's memorial of self-explanation likewise long went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: while the southern evaluation and Tongheng's explanatory memorial likewise languished without response for a long time.

sentences.zh: 同亨適給由入都，遂引疾。

translations.literal: Tongheng happened to enter the capital to receive his credentials and thereupon pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Tongheng happened to be in the capital to receive his credentials and took the occasion to plead illness.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: An edict granted him the additional title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him senior guardian of the heir apparent and let him retire.

sentences.zh: 同亨初入吏部，嚴嵩其鄉人，尚書吳鵬則父同年也，同亨無私謁。

translations.literal: When Tongheng first entered the Ministry of Personnel, Yan Song was his townsman and Minister Wu Peng had been his father's examination-year mate, yet Tongheng made no private visits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his Ministry of Personnel career, despite Yan Song being a fellow townsman and Minister Wu Peng having been his father's jinshi cohort, Tongheng never paid them private calls.

sentences.zh: 嘗止宿署舍，彌月不歸。

translations.literal: He once stayed overnight at the office and did not return home for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: He would sometimes sleep at his office and not go home for an entire month.

sentences.zh: 雅與羅汝芳、耿定向善。

translations.literal: He was on excellent terms with Luo Rufang and Geng Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with the scholars Luo Rufang and Geng Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 尚書楊博痛詆偽儒，同亨曰：「此中多暗修，非可概斥。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Bo bitterly denounced false Confucians; Tongheng said, "Among them many pursue the Way in secret; they cannot all be dismissed outright.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Yang Bo lashed out at self-styled Confucians, Tongheng replied, "Many among them cultivate virtue quietly—they cannot be condemned wholesale.

sentences.zh: 即使陽假名義，視呈身進取、恬不知恥者，孰愈哉？」

translations.literal: Even if they merely put on a show under false names, compared with those who crassly thrust themselves forward for advancement without the least shame, which is worse?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if some wear virtue as a mask, are they not still preferable to men who scramble for promotion without a shred of shame?"

sentences.zh: 卒年七十有五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚恭端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Gongduan ("Respectful and Upright").
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made junior guardian and given the posthumous name Gongduan, "Respectful and Upright."

sentences.zh: 弟乾亨，字於健。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qianheng, courtesy name Yujian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qianheng, styled Yujian.

sentences.zh: 從羅洪先學。

translations.literal: He studied under Luo Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of Luo Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 登萬歷五年進士，除合肥知縣，調休寧。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was appointed Magistrate of Hefei, and transferred to Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Wanli 5, he became magistrate of Hefei and was then moved to Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 擢御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor.

sentences.zh: 給事中馮景劾李成梁被謫，乾亨以尚書張學顏右成梁也，並劾之。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Feng Jing impeached Li Chengliang and was demoted; Qianheng, because Minister Zhang Xueyan favored Chengliang, impeached both of them.
translations.idiomatic: After the supervising secretary Feng Jing impeached Li Chengliang and was punished, Qianheng—seeing that Minister Zhang Xueyan was shielding Chengliang—impeached them both.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，黜為海州判官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and demoted him to Assistant Magistrate of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor demoted him to assistant magistrate of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷大名推官，歷光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to investigating magistrate of Daming and served successively as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He worked his way back up to investigating magistrate of Daming and eventually became vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十八年冬，敕兼監察御史，閱視大同邊務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year, by imperial order he also served as Censor and inspected border affairs at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 18, he was commissioned as censor to inspect border affairs at Datong.

sentences.zh: 劾罷總兵官以下十余人。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed more than ten persons including the commander-in-chief and those below.
translations.idiomatic: His impeachments forced out the regional commander and more than a dozen subordinates.

sentences.zh: 大同士兵歲餉萬二千石，兵自征之，民不勝擾。

translations.literal: Datong local soldiers received ten thousand two hundred shi of annual rations; the soldiers collected them themselves, and the people could not bear the harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Datong's local troops drew 12,000 shi in annual pay, but the soldiers collected it themselves, and civilians were crushed by the exactions.

sentences.zh: 乾亨議留兵二百，余盡汰之。

translations.literal: Qianheng proposed retaining two hundred soldiers and cutting all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Qianheng proposed keeping only 200 men and disbanding the rest.

sentences.zh: 屢奏邊備事宜，輒中機要。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on border defense matters and always hit what was essential.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated memorials on frontier defense consistently struck at the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 諸武弁之詬同亨也，大學士王家屏遣諭之曰：「天下有叛軍，寧有叛臣？

translations.literal: When the military officers abused Tongheng, Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping sent someone to instruct them, saying, "Under Heaven there may be mutinous troops—can there be mutinous ministers?
translations.idiomatic: When officers hounded Tongheng, Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping sent this warning: "Armies may mutiny—will ministers?

sentences.zh: 若曹於禁地辱大臣，罪且死。」

translations.literal: You lot insult a high minister within the forbidden precinct—your crime merits death."
translations.idiomatic: For you to humiliate a senior minister inside the forbidden precinct is a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 諸人乃散去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the men dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd then broke up.

sentences.zh: 尚書石星言貴臣被辱，大傷國體，給事中鐘羽正亦言之。

translations.literal: Minister Shi Xing said that a noble minister had been insulted, greatly harming the dignity of the state; the Supervising Secretary Zhong Yuzheng also spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shi Xing argued that the assault on a senior official had shamed the realm, and supervising secretary Zhong Yuzheng said the same.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action.

sentences.zh: 家屏密揭力爭，乃奪掌後府定國公徐文璧祿半歲，而治首事者以法。

translations.literal: Jiaping forcefully argued in a secret memorial and thereupon stripped Duke Dingguo Xu Wenbi, who controlled the rear palace office, of half a year's salary, and punished the ringleaders according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiaping pressed the case in a secret memorial, and the court finally docked Duke Xu Wenbi of the Rear Palace Office half a year's stipend while prosecuting the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 乾亨尋進大理丞，遷少卿。

translations.literal: Qianheng soon advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Revision and was promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Qianheng was soon promoted to vice director of the Court of Revision and then to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 考功郎趙南星以考察事被斥，乾亨論救，侵執政，復移書辨之。

translations.literal: The Evaluation Director Zhao Nanxing was dismissed over evaluation matters; Qianheng memorialized in his defense, offending the chief ministers, and again sent a letter arguing the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Nanxing, director of evaluations, was ousted in a personnel review, Qianheng defended him—crossing the chief ministers—and followed up with a letter rebutting them.

sentences.zh: 廷推巡撫者三，俱不用。

translations.literal: Three candidates for grand coordinator were recommended at court; none were used.
translations.idiomatic: Three times the court nominated him for a provincial governorship, and each time the appointment went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 遂引疾歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: He thereupon pleaded illness and returned home; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 乾亨言行不茍，與其兄並以名德稱。

translations.literal: Qianheng's words and conduct were scrupulous; he and his elder brother were both famed for integrity and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous in word and deed, Qianheng and his brother were alike celebrated for moral stature.

sentences.zh: 辛自修，字子吉，襄城人。

translations.literal: Xin Zixiu, courtesy name Ziji, was a man of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zixiu, styled Ziji, was from Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1556.

sentences.zh: 除海寧知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Haining.

sentences.zh: 擢吏科給事中，奏言：「吏部銓註，遴才要矣，量地尤急。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Department of Personnel Affairs and memorialized: "In the Ministry of Personnel's appointments, selecting talent is essential, but gauging locality is especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary in the personnel department, he wrote: "When the Ministry of Personnel fills posts, finding the right talent matters—but matching men to place matters even more.

sentences.zh: 邇京府屬吏以大計去者十之五，豈畿輦下獨多不肖哉？

translations.literal: Recently among subordinate officials of the capital prefectures, half of those removed in the grand evaluation came from there—are there alone so many unworthy men under the imperial chariot?
translations.idiomatic: In the last grand evaluation, half the capital prefectures' junior officials were removed—surely the capital is not uniquely full of incompetents?

sentences.zh: 地艱而事猥也。

translations.literal: The locality is hard and the business is petty.
translations.idiomatic: The posts are grinding and the work is thankless.

sentences.zh: 請量地劇易以除官，量事繁簡以註考。」

translations.literal: I request measuring the severity or ease of localities when appointing officials, and measuring the complexity or simplicity of duties when recording evaluations."
translations.idiomatic: Assign officials according to whether the locality is taxing or easy, and grade evaluations according to whether the duties are heavy or light."

sentences.zh: 吏部善其言，請令撫按舉劾如自修議。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel approved his words and requested that grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners report and impeach as Xin Zixiu proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel endorsed his proposal and asked provincial governors and censors to impeach according to his scheme.

sentences.zh: 巡視京營，劾典營務鎮遠侯顧寰、協理僉都御史李燧，請戒寰罷燧。

translations.literal: Inspecting the capital garrisons, he impeached Gu Huan, Marquis of Zhenyuan, who managed garrison affairs, and Li Sui, Censor-in-Chief on joint duty, requesting that Huan be warned and Sui dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the capital garrisons, he impeached Marquis Gu Huan of Zhenyuan, who ran garrison affairs, and censor-in-chief Li Sui, who assisted him, asking that Huan be admonished and Sui removed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 歷遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Department of Rites Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary in the rites department.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延不法，自修極論其奸。

translations.literal: Earl of Chengyi Liu Shiyan was lawless; Zixiu thoroughly denounced his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: When Earl Liu Shiyan of Chengyi broke the law, Zixiu exposed his misconduct in full.

sentences.zh: 詔革任禁錮。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his appointment and placed him under house confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revoked his title and put him under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，給事中胡應嘉言事斥，自修疏救。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, the Supervising Secretary Hu Yingjia was dismissed for speaking on state affairs; Zixiu memorialized in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1, when supervising secretary Hu Yingjia was punished for remonstrating, Zixiu defended him in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，論奪尚書顧可學、徐可成，侍郎朱隆禧、郭文英贈謚；

translations.literal: Before long, he argued for stripping the posthumous titles and ennoblements of the Ministers Gu Kexue and Xu Kecheng and the Vice Ministers Zhu Longxi and Guo Wenying;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he argued that posthumous honors should be revoked from ministers Gu Kexue and Xu Kecheng and vice ministers Zhu Longxi and Guo Wenying;

sentences.zh: 以可成由黃冠，文英由工匠，可學、隆禧俱以方藥進也。

translations.literal: because Kecheng had come from among Daoist priests, Wenying from artisans, and Kexue and Longxi had both risen through submitting elixirs.
translations.idiomatic: Kecheng had been a Daoist priest, Wenying a craftsman, and Kexue and Longxi had both curried favor by supplying elixirs.

sentences.zh: 擢太仆少卿，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of the imperial stud, he then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 萬歷六年，起應天府丞，再遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli, he was recalled as Vice Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture and again promoted to Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6 he was recalled as vice prefect of Yingtian and later promoted to minister of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 以右僉都御史巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: As Right Censor-in-Chief he served as Grand Coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: As right censor-in-chief he governed the six prefectures of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 奏減均徭裏甲銀六萬兩，增築雄、任丘二縣堤，以禦滹沱水患。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the combined corvée and lijia silver by sixty thousand taels and to extend dikes in Xiong and Renqiu counties to guard against the disasters of the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: He secured a cut of 60,000 taels in combined corvée and lijia levies and had dikes built in Xiong and Renqiu counties to hold back flooding on the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 每歲防秋，巡撫移駐易州，征所部供費，防秋已罷，征如故，自修奏已之。

translations.literal: Each year during autumn defense, the grand coordinator moved his headquarters to Yizhou and levied supplies and expenses from his subordinates; after autumn defense ended the levies continued as before; Zixiu memorialized to stop this.
translations.idiomatic: Every autumn defense season, governors moved to Yizhou and taxed their jurisdictions for supplies—and kept taxing even after the season ended; Zixiu got the practice stopped.

sentences.zh: 入歷大理卿，兵部左、右侍郎，擢南京右都御史。

translations.literal: He entered service successively as Minister of Revision, Left and Right Vice Minister of War, and was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the Court of Revision, then as left and right vice minister of war, and was finally promoted to right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 御史沈汝梁者，巡視下江，用饋遺為名，盡括所部贖鍰，自修劾奏之。

translations.literal: The Censor Shen Ruliang, while inspecting the lower Yangzi region, under the name of presenting gifts collected all fines from redemption payments within his jurisdiction; Zixiu impeached and memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Shen Ruliang, inspecting the lower Yangzi, seized every fine in his circuit under the pretense of accepting gifts; Zixiu impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲懲貪吏，乃命逮治汝梁，而召自修為左都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then wanting to punish corrupt officials; he therefore ordered Shen Ruliang arrested and prosecuted, and summoned Zixiu to serve as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to crack down on corruption, the emperor ordered Shen Ruliang arrested—and summoned Zixiu to become left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大計京官，政府欲庇私人，去異己。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, during the grand evaluation of capital officials, the chief ministers wished to protect their own men and remove those who differed from them.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 15, during the capital officials' grand evaluation, the cabinet wanted to shield allies and purge dissenters.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書楊巍承意指惟謹，自修患之，先期上奏，請勿以愛憎為喜怒，排抑孤立之人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Personnel Yang Wei followed their intent with extreme caution; Zixiu was troubled by this and beforehand submitted a memorial requesting that evaluations not be swayed by likes and dislikes, nor used to suppress isolated men.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yang Wei read the cabinet's wishes all too faithfully, so Zixiu filed an advance memorial urging that evaluations not be driven by favoritism or used to isolate opponents.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，而政府不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, but the chief ministers were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, but the cabinet was displeased.

sentences.zh: 有貪競者十余輩，皆政府所厚，自修欲去之。

translations.literal: More than ten men who were greedy and contentious, all favored by the chief ministers, Zixiu wished to remove.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen grasping officials favored by the cabinet were targets Zixiu wanted removed.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳與郊自度不免，遂言憲臣將以一眚棄人，一舉空國。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao, judging himself could not escape, then said the censor-in-chief would discard men over a single fault and in one stroke empty the state.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Chen Yujiao, sensing he would not escape, charged that the censor-in-chief would ruin careers over a single misstep and gut the government at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 於是自修所欲斥者悉獲免。

translations.literal: Thereupon all those Zixiu wished to dismiss were entirely spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, every official Zixiu had meant to dismiss was spared.

sentences.zh: 已而御史張鳴岡等拾遺，首工部尚書何起鳴。

translations.literal: Before long the Censors Zhang Minggang and others, during the supplementary review, began with Minister of Works He Qiming.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censors including Zhang Minggang, in a supplementary review, opened their list with Minister of Works He Qiming.

sentences.zh: 起鳴故以督工與中官張誠厚，而雅不善自修，遂訐自修挾仇主使。

translations.literal: Qiming had long been close to the eunuch Zhang Cheng through supervising construction work, and he had never gotten along with Zixiu; he therefore accused Zixiu of harboring a grudge and masterminding the impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: Qiming owed his standing to the eunuch Zhang Cheng through construction work and had long disliked Zixiu; he now accused Zixiu of orchestrating the charges out of private spite.

sentences.zh: 與郊及給事中吳之佳助之。

translations.literal: Chen Yujiao and the Supervising Secretary Wu Zhijia assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yujiao and supervising secretary Wu Zhijia lent their support.

sentences.zh: 御史高維崧、趙卿、張鳴岡、左之宜不平，劾起鳴飾非詭辨。

translations.literal: The Censors Gao Weisong, Zhao Qing, Zhang Minggang, and Zuo Zhiyi, resentful, impeached Qiming for covering faults with specious arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Gao Weisong, Zhao Qing, Zhang Minggang, and Zuo Zhiyi, taking offense, impeached Qiming for glossing over his faults with specious arguments.

sentences.zh: 帝先入張誠言，頗疑自修。

translations.literal: The emperor, having first taken Zhang Cheng's word, was quite suspicious of Zixiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already been swayed by Zhang Cheng and grew quite suspicious of Zixiu.

sentences.zh: 得疏益不悅，曰：「朝廷每用一人，言官輒紛紛排擊。

translations.literal: Receiving the memorial, he grew even more displeased and said: "Whenever the court appoints someone, the remonstrating officials at once swarm to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial only deepened his displeasure. He said, "Every time the court appoints a man, the remonstrating officials swarm to tear him down.

sentences.zh: 今起鳴去，爾等舉堪此任者。」

translations.literal: Now that Qiming is to go, you name someone fit for this post."
translations.idiomatic: Qiming is leaving—name someone among you who is fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 維崧等具疏引罪，無他舉。

translations.literal: Gao Weisong and the others submitted full memorials accepting blame and proposed no one else.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Weisong and the others submitted full memorials accepting blame and nominated no one else.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，悉出之外。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger sent them all out to outer posts.
translations.idiomatic: In anger the emperor sent them all out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中張養蒙申救，亦奪俸。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Zhang Yangmeng pleaded on their behalf and also had his salary withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhang Yangmeng interceded on their behalf and also had his salary withheld.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事王德新復疏爭，語侵嬖幸。

translations.literal: Wang Dexin, a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, submitted another memorial disputing the matter; his language encroached on the favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dexin, a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, submitted another memorial disputing the matter in language that encroached on the emperor's favorites.

sentences.zh: 帝下之詔獄，酷刑究主者。

translations.literal: The emperor sent him to the imperial prison and used brutal torture to investigate the mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him thrown into the imperial prison and tortured brutally to uncover the mastermind.

sentences.zh: 無所承，乃削其籍。

translations.literal: He confessed nothing; the emperor therefore struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed to nothing, so the emperor struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 自修不自安，亟引疾歸。

translations.literal: Zixiu himself felt insecure and urgently pleaded illness to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu himself no longer felt secure and urgently pleaded illness to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 自修之進也，非執政意，故不為所容。

translations.literal: Zixiu's advancement had not been the chief ministers' intent, so he was not tolerated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu's rise had never been the cabinet's wish, and they would not tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 久之，起南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After some time, he was raised to Minister of Justice in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled as minister of justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 復以工部尚書召。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned to serve as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未上，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚肅敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Su Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Su Min.

sentences.zh: 德新，安福人，後起官至光祿丞。

translations.literal: Dexin was a native of Anfu; later he rose to the post of vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin was a native of Anfu; he later rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 溫純，字景文，三原人。

translations.literal: Wen Chun, styled Jingwen, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Chun, styled Jingwen, was a native of Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing 44.

sentences.zh: 由壽光知縣征為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Shouguang he was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Household section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as magistrate of Shouguang he was summoned to serve as a supervising secretary in the Household section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，穆宗既禫除，猶不與大臣接。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, although Emperor Muzong had completed the end of mourning, he still did not receive the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3, though Emperor Muzong had completed the end of mourning, he still would not receive the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 純請遵祖制延訪群工，親決章奏，報聞。

translations.literal: Chun requested adherence to ancestral precedent in summoning and consulting officials and personally deciding memorials; the request was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: Chun urged that ancestral precedent be followed—officials summoned for consultation, memorials decided in person—and the court acknowledged his request.

sentences.zh: 屢遷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Military section.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he became chief supervising secretary of the Military section.

sentences.zh: 倭陷廣東廣海衛，大殺掠而去。

translations.literal: Wokou captured Guangdong's Guanghai Guard, killed and plundered extensively, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wokou took Guangdong's Guanghai Guard, slaughtered and plundered on a great scale, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 總兵劉燾以戰卻聞，純劾燾欺罔。

translations.literal: The regional commander Liu Tao reported he had fought them off; Chun impeached Tao for deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Liu Tao reported that he had fought the raiders off; Chun impeached him for deception.

sentences.zh: 時方召燾督京營，遂置不問。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Tao was just being summoned to command the capital garrison, so the matter was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao was then being summoned to command the capital garrison, so the matter was set aside without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐朝弼有罪，詔許其子襲爵。

translations.literal: The Duke of Qian, Mu Chaobi, was guilty; an edict permitted his son to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qian, Mu Chaobi, had been found guilty, yet an edict permitted his son to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 純言事未竟，不當遽襲。

translations.literal: Chun argued the case was unresolved and the succession should not be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that the case was still unresolved and the succession should not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 中官陳洪請封其父母，純執不可。

translations.literal: The eunuch Chen Hong requested ennoblement of his parents; Chun held firm that it was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Hong petitioned to have his parents ennobled; Chun held firm that it could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 言官李已、石星獲譴，疏救之。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials Li Yi and Shi Xing were punished; he memorialized to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When the remonstrating officials Li Yi and Shi Xing were punished, he memorialized to save them.

sentences.zh: 初，趙貞吉更營制，三營各統一大將。

translations.literal: Initially Zhao Zhenji reformed the garrison system: each of the three camps would be under one great general.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhao Zhenji reformed the garrison system so that each of the three camps would answer to one great general.

sentences.zh: 以恭順侯吳繼爵典五軍，而都督袁正、焦澤典神樞、神機。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jijue was put in charge of the Five Armies, while the commanders-in-chief Yuan Zheng and Jiao Ze commanded the Divine Pivot and Divine Engine corps.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Jijue, was placed in charge of the Five Armies, while commanders-in-chief Yuan Zheng and Jiao Ze took the Divine Pivot and Divine Engine corps.

sentences.zh: 繼爵恥與同列，固辭。

translations.literal: Jijue felt ashamed to stand as equals and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jijue was ashamed to serve as an equal and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝為罷二人，盡易以勛臣。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed the two men for his sake and replaced them entirely with meritorious nobles.
translations.idiomatic: For his sake the emperor dismissed the two men and replaced them entirely with meritorious nobles.

sentences.zh: 純請廣求將才，毋拘世爵，不納。

translations.literal: Chun requested broad search for martial talent without restricting to hereditary titles; the request was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Chun urged a broad search for military talent without limiting appointments to hereditary titles; the court did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 已，復命文臣三人分督之，時號「六提督」。

translations.literal: Later three civil officials were again ordered to share command; they were called at the time "the six grand coordinators."
translations.idiomatic: Later three civil officials were again ordered to share command with them, and the six were known at the time as "the six grand coordinators."

sentences.zh: 純以政令多門，極陳不便，遂復舊制。

translations.literal: Chun argued that too many hands held authority and spoke at length on the inconvenience; the old system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that authority was split too many ways and spoke at length on the harm this caused, and the old system was restored.

sentences.zh: 俺答請貢市，高拱定議許之。

translations.literal: Altan Khan requested tribute trade; Gao Gong fixed policy to permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan requested tribute trade, and Gao Gong settled policy to permit it.

sentences.zh: 純以為弛邊備，非中國利。

translations.literal: Chun held that this would slacken frontier defenses and was not to China's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Chun held that this would slacken frontier defenses and was not to China's advantage.

sentences.zh: 出為湖廣參政，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was sent out as administration vice commissioner of Huguang and pleaded illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administration vice commissioner of Huguang and pleaded illness to return home.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，用薦起河南參議。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli's reign, on recommendation he was raised to administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wanli reign, on recommendation he was recalled as administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以大理卿改兵部右侍郎兼右副都御史，巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, from president of the Court of Judicial Review he was transferred to vice minister of War and right vice censor-in-chief, with charge as grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 12 he moved from president of the Court of Judicial Review to vice minister of war and right vice censor-in-chief, with charge as grand coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部左侍郎，進右副都御史，督倉場。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as left vice minister of Revenue, advanced to right vice censor-in-chief, and supervised the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as left vice minister of revenue, was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief, and supervised the granaries.

sentences.zh: 母憂去。

translations.literal: He left on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 進南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of personnel in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 父老，乞養歸。

translations.literal: His father was old; he requested leave to care for him and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: His father was old; he asked leave to care for him and returned home.

sentences.zh: 終喪，召為左都御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was summoned as left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was summoned to serve as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 礦稅使四出，有司逮系累累，純極論其害，請盡釋之，不報。

translations.literal: Mining-tax envoys went out in all directions; local officials arrested and detained people in droves; Chun spoke at length on the harm and requested full release; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Mining-tax envoys fanned out in all directions, and local officials arrested people in droves; Chun spoke at length on the harm and asked that all be released—there was no response.

sentences.zh: 已，諸閹益橫，所至剽奪，汙人婦女。

translations.literal: Before long the eunuchs grew more overbearing; wherever they went they plundered and violated women.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuchs grew more overbearing still; wherever they went they plundered and violated women.

sentences.zh: 四方無賴奸人蜂起言利：有請開雲南塞外寶井者；

translations.literal: Scoundrels from all quarters swarmed forward proposing profit schemes: some petitioned to open the treasure mines beyond Yunnan's frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: Scoundrels from every quarter swarmed forward with schemes for profit: some petitioned to open the treasure mines beyond Yunnan's frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 或又言海外呂宋國有機易山，素產金銀，歲可得金十萬、銀三十萬；

translations.literal: others spoke of Mount Jiyi in Luzon overseas, said always to produce gold and silver, yielding one hundred thousand taels of gold and three hundred thousand taels of silver yearly;
translations.idiomatic: others spoke of Mount Jiyi in Luzon overseas, said always to produce gold and silver and to yield one hundred thousand taels of gold and three hundred thousand taels of silver each year;

sentences.zh: 或言淮、揚饒鹽利，用其筴，歲可得銀五十萬。

translations.literal: others spoke of salt profits in Huai and Yang, saying that by their plan five hundred thousand taels of silver could be obtained yearly.
translations.idiomatic: others spoke of the rich salt profits of Huai and Yang, saying that by their plan five hundred thousand taels of silver could be obtained each year.

sentences.zh: 帝並欣然納之，遠近駭震。

translations.literal: The emperor gladly accepted all of them; near and far were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly accepted them all, and alarm spread near and far.

sentences.zh: 純言：「緬人方伺隙，寶井一開，兵端必起。

translations.literal: Chun said: "The Burmese are just watching for an opening; once the treasure mines are opened, war will surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "The Burmese are watching for an opening; once the treasure mines are opened, war will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 余元俊一鹽犯，數千贓不能輸，而欲得五十萬金，將安取之？

translations.literal: Yu Yuanjun is but a salt smuggler who cannot even pay several thousand in ill-gotten gains—yet he wants five hundred thousand taels; where does he expect to get them?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuanjun is nothing but a salt smuggler who cannot even pay off several thousand in illicit gains—yet he wants five hundred thousand taels; where does he expect to get them?

sentences.zh: 機易山在海外，必無遍地金銀，任人往取；

translations.literal: Mount Jiyi is overseas; there certainly cannot be gold and silver spread across the land for anyone to take;
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jiyi lies overseas; there cannot be gold and silver spread across the land for anyone to take at will;

sentences.zh: 不過假借詔旨，闌出禁物與番人市易，利歸群小，害貽國家。

translations.literal: it is nothing but borrowing imperial orders to smuggle contraband out and trade with foreigners—the profit goes to petty men, the harm falls on the state.
translations.idiomatic: this is nothing but a pretext to smuggle contraband out under imperial orders and trade with foreigners—the profit goes to petty men, the harm falls on the state.

sentences.zh: 乞盡捕諸奸人，付臣等行法，而亟撤稅監之害民者。」

translations.literal: I beg that all these villains be arrested and handed to us for punishment, and that the tax supervisors harming the people be swiftly withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all these villains be arrested and handed to us for punishment, and that the tax supervisors harming the people be swiftly withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: There was no response either.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 當是時，中外爭請罷礦稅，帝悉置不省。

translations.literal: At that time, court and country alike clamored to abolish mining taxes; the emperor ignored them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court and country alike clamored to abolish mining taxes, and the emperor ignored them all.
