sentences.zh: 純等憂懼不知所出，乃倡諸大臣伏闕泣請。

translations.literal: Chun and the others, anxious and at their wits' end, then proposed that the chief ministers kneel weeping at the palace gate to petition.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and the others, anxious and at their wits' end, then proposed that the chief ministers kneel weeping at the palace gate to petition.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，問誰倡者，對曰：「都御史臣純。」

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and asked who had proposed it; they answered: "Left Censor-in-Chief, your subject Chun."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and asked who had proposed it; they answered, "Left Censor-in-Chief, your subject Chun."

sentences.zh: 帝為霽威，遣人慰諭曰：「疏且下。」

translations.literal: The emperor's rage softened; he sent someone to comfort them, saying: "The memorial will soon be issued."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage softened; he sent someone to comfort them, saying, "The memorial will soon be issued."

sentences.zh: 乃退。

translations.literal: They then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而卒不行。

translations.literal: In the end it was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 廣東李鳳、陜西梁永、雲南楊榮並以礦稅激民變，純又抗言：「稅使竊弄陛下威福以十計，參隨憑藉稅使聲勢以百計，地方奸民竄身為參隨爪牙以萬計。

translations.literal: Li Feng of Guangdong, Liang Yong of Shaanxi, and Yang Rong of Yunnan all stirred popular rebellion through mining taxes; Chun again spoke boldly: "Tax envoys who usurp Your Majesty's authority number in the tens; attendants who rely on the tax envoys' power number in the hundreds; local scoundrels who attach themselves as the attendants' claws and teeth number in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng of Guangdong, Liang Yong of Shaanxi, and Yang Rong of Yunnan all stirred popular rebellion through mining taxes; Chun again spoke boldly: "Tax envoys who usurp Your Majesty's authority number in the tens; attendants who rely on the tax envoys' power number in the hundreds; local scoundrels who attach themselves as the attendants' claws and teeth number in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 宇內生靈困於水旱，困於采辦、營運、轉輸，既囂然喪其樂生之心，安能復勝此千萬虎狼耶！

translations.literal: All living souls within the realm are afflicted by flood and drought, afflicted by procurement, transport operations, and relay duties—already noisy with the loss of their will to live; how can they again withstand these millions of wolves and tigers!
translations.idiomatic: All living souls within the realm are already afflicted by flood and drought, by procurement, transport operations, and relay duties—they have lost the will to live in uproar; how can they again withstand these millions of wolves and tigers!

sentences.zh: 願即日罷礦稅，逮鳳等置於理。」

translations.literal: I pray that mining taxes be abolished this very day and Feng and the others arrested and brought to justice."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that mining taxes be abolished this very day and that Feng and the others be arrested and brought to justice."

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: There was no response either.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史顧龍楨巡按廣東，與布政使王泮語不合，起毆之，泮即棄官去。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Censor Gu Longzhen, on inspection tour in Guangdong, had words that did not accord with Administration Commissioner Wang Pan; he rose and beat him; Pan immediately abandoned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, censor Gu Longzhen, on inspection tour in Guangdong, quarreled with administration commissioner Wang Pan, rose and beat him, and Pan immediately abandoned his post and left.

sentences.zh: 純劾罷龍楨。

translations.literal: Chun impeached and had Longzhen dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chun impeached him and had Longzhen dismissed.

sentences.zh: 御史於永清按陜西貪，懼純舉奏，倡同列救龍楨，顯與純異，以脅制純，又與都給事中姚文蔚比而傾純。

translations.literal: The Censor Yu Yongqing, inspecting Shaanxi and corrupt, feared Chun would impeach him; he incited his colleagues to save Longzhen, openly siding against Chun to intimidate him; he also joined with Chief Supervising Secretary Yao Wenwei to undermine Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Yongqing, inspecting Shaanxi and corrupt, feared Chun would impeach him; he incited his colleagues to save Longzhen, openly siding against Chun to intimidate him, and also joined with chief supervising secretary Yao Wenwei to undermine Chun.

sentences.zh: 純不勝憤，上疏盡發永清交構狀，並及文蔚，語頗侵首輔沈一貫。

translations.literal: Chun, unable to contain his anger, memorialized exposing Yongqing's manipulations fully, also implicating Wenwei; his language somewhat encroached on Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, unable to contain his anger, memorialized exposing Yongqing's manipulations in full and also implicating Wenwei; his language somewhat encroached on chief grand secretary Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 一貫等疏辨。

translations.literal: Yiguan and others memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan and others memorialized in defense.

sentences.zh: 帝為下永清、文蔚二疏，而純劾疏留不下。

translations.literal: The emperor issued the two memorials from Yongqing and Wenwei, but kept Chun's impeachment memorial withheld.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued the memorials from Yongqing and Wenwei, but kept Chun's impeachment memorial withheld.

sentences.zh: 純益憤，三疏論之，因力丐罷，乃謫永清。

translations.literal: Chun grew angrier; three memorials debated the matter; through forceful pleading for dismissal, Yongqing was finally demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Chun grew angrier still; he submitted three memorials debating the matter and forcefully pleaded to be dismissed, and only then was Yongqing demoted.

sentences.zh: 純遂與一貫忤。

translations.literal: Chun thus came into conflict with Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun thus came into open conflict with Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳治則、鐘兆鬥皆一貫私人，先後劾純。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretaries Chen Zheze and Zhong Zhaodou, both Yiguan's men, impeached Chun in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Chen Zheze and Zhong Zhaodou, both Yiguan's men, impeached Chun in succession.

sentences.zh: 御史湯兆京不平，疏斥其妄。

translations.literal: The Censor Tang Zhaojing, resentful, memorialized denouncing them as reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Zhaojing, taking offense, memorialized denouncing them as reckless.

sentences.zh: 純求去，章二十上，杜門者九閱月。

translations.literal: Chun sought to leave; twenty memorials were submitted; he shut his doors for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Chun sought to leave; he submitted twenty memorials and shut his doors for nine months.

sentences.zh: 帝雅重純，諭留之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long held Chun in esteem and ordered him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long held Chun in esteem and ordered him to remain.

sentences.zh: 純不得已，強起視事。

translations.literal: Chun had no choice but to force himself to rise and attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had no choice but to force himself to rise and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 及妖書事起，力為沈鯉、郭正域辨誣。

translations.literal: When the "demonic book" affair arose, he vigorously defended Shen Li and Guo Zhengyu against false charges.
translations.idiomatic: When the "demonic book" affair arose, he vigorously defended Shen Li and Guo Zhengyu against false charges.

sentences.zh: 楚宗人戕殺撫臣，純復言無反狀。

translations.literal: When a clansman of Chu killed the grand coordinator, Chun again argued there was no sign of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When a clansman of Chu killed the grand coordinator, Chun again argued that there was no sign of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 一貫怨益深。

translations.literal: Yiguan's resentment grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan's resentment grew deeper still.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，大計京朝官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the grand evaluation of capital officials was held.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 32 the grand evaluation of capital officials was held.

sentences.zh: 純與吏部侍郎楊時喬主之，一貫所欲庇者兆鬥及錢夢臯等皆在謫中。

translations.literal: Chun and Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao presided; those Yiguan wished to protect—Zhong Zhaodou and Qian Menggao among others—were all listed for censure.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and vice minister of personnel Yang Shiqiao presided; those Yiguan wished to protect—Zhong Zhaodou and Qian Menggao among others—were all listed for censure.

sentences.zh: 疏入久之，忽降旨切責，盡留被察科道官，而察疏仍不下。

translations.literal: Long after the memorial entered, an edict suddenly descended with sharp rebuke, retaining all the censored remonstrating officials, while the evaluation memorial still was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Long after the memorial entered, an edict suddenly descended with sharp rebuke, retaining all the censured remonstrating officials, while the evaluation memorial still was not issued.

sentences.zh: 純求去益力。

translations.literal: Chun pleaded to leave with greater force.
translations.idiomatic: Chun pleaded to leave with greater force.

sentences.zh: 夢臯、兆鬥既得留，則連章訐純楚事。

translations.literal: Menggao and Zhaodou, having been retained, then submitted successive memorials attacking Chun over the Chu affair.
translations.idiomatic: Menggao and Zhaodou, having been retained, then submitted successive memorials attacking Chun over the Chu affair.

sentences.zh: 言純曲庇叛人，且誣以納賄。

translations.literal: They said Chun had bent the law to protect a rebel and further slandered him with taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: They said Chun had bent the law to protect a rebel and further slandered him with taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 廷臣大駭，爭劾夢臯等。

translations.literal: Court officials were greatly alarmed and competed to impeach Menggao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were greatly alarmed and competed to impeach Menggao and the others.

sentences.zh: 夢臯等亦再疏劾純求勝。

translations.literal: Menggao and the others also submitted further memorials impeaching Chun, seeking victory.
translations.idiomatic: Menggao and the others also submitted further memorials impeaching Chun, seeking to prevail.

sentences.zh: 俱留中。

translations.literal: All were kept withheld.
translations.idiomatic: All were kept withheld.

sentences.zh: 已，南京給事中陳嘉訓等極論二人陰有所恃，朋比作奸，當亟斥之，而聽純歸，以全大臣之體。

translations.literal: Before long, the Supervising Secretaries in Nanjing including Chen Jiaxun argued forcefully that the two had secret backing, formed factions to do evil, and should be swiftly expelled, while Chun should be allowed to return home to preserve the dignity owed a grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, supervising secretaries in Nanjing including Chen Jiaxun argued forcefully that the two had secret backing, formed factions to do evil, and should be swiftly expelled, while Chun should be allowed to return home to preserve the dignity owed a grand minister.

sentences.zh: 帝竟批夢臯等前疏，予純致仕，夢臯、兆鬥亦罷歸。

translations.literal: The emperor finally endorsed the earlier memorials of Menggao and the others, granted Chun retirement, and Menggao and Zhaodou were also dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally endorsed the earlier memorials of Menggao and the others, granted Chun retirement, and Menggao and Zhaodou were also dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 純清白奉公。

translations.literal: Chun served the public with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chun served the public with integrity.

sentences.zh: 五主南北考察，澄汰悉當。

translations.literal: Five times he presided over evaluations north and south; his clearings and dismissals were all apt.
translations.idiomatic: Five times he presided over evaluations north and south, and his clearings and dismissals were all apt.

sentences.zh: 肅百僚，振風紀，時稱名臣。

translations.literal: He disciplined the hundred officials and restored discipline; he was called at the time a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined the hundred officials and restored discipline, and was acclaimed at the time as a great minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚恭毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously given the epithet Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously ennobled with the epithet Gongyi, "Respectful and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 趙世卿，字象賢，歷城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shiqing, style name Xiangxian, was a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiqing, styled Xiangxian, was from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Principal Clerk in the Ministry of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 張居正當國，政尚嚴。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng held the state, government favored strictness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng dominated the government, policy favored strictness.

sentences.zh: 州縣學取士不得過十五人；

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties in selecting scholars could not exceed fifteen persons;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county schools were limited to selecting no more than fifteen scholars;

sentences.zh: 布按二司以下官，雖公事毋許乘驛馬；

translations.literal: Officials from the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions downward, even on public business were not permitted to ride relay horses;
translations.idiomatic: Officials below the rank of provincial administration and surveillance commissioners were barred from using relay horses even on official business;

sentences.zh: 大辟之刑，歲有定額；

translations.literal: Capital punishments had a fixed annual quota;
translations.idiomatic: The death penalty was subject to a fixed annual quota;

sentences.zh: 征賦以九分為率，有司不及格者罰；

translations.literal: Tax collection took nine parts in ten as the standard, and officials who fell short were punished;
translations.idiomatic: Tax collection was held to a nine-tenths rate, and local officials who failed to meet it were penalized;

sentences.zh: 又數重譴言事者。

translations.literal: Moreover he repeatedly punished heavily those who spoke on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly meted out heavy punishment to memorialists.

sentences.zh: 世卿奏匡時五要。

translations.literal: Shiqing memorialized on five essentials for correcting the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing submitted a memorial outlining five essentials for setting the age right.

sentences.zh: 請廣取士之額，寬驛傳之禁，省大辟，緩催科，而末極論言路當開，言：「近者臺諫習為脂韋，以希世取寵。

translations.literal: He requested expanding the quota for selecting scholars, loosening restrictions on relay transport, reducing capital punishments, and easing tax collection; at the end he argued at length that the avenue of speech should be opened, saying: "Recently censorate and remonstrance officials have grown accustomed to being oleaginous and ingratiating, seeking worldly favor to win the sovereign's affection.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that scholar quotas be expanded, relay-horse restrictions relaxed, capital sentences reduced, and tax collection slowed; he ended with a lengthy argument that the avenue of speech must be reopened, declaring: "Recently, censorate and remonstrance officials have fallen into the habit of oleaginous flattery, currying favor to win the throne's regard.

sentences.zh: 事關軍國，卷舌無聲。

translations.literal: When affairs concerned army and state, they rolled their tongues and were silent.
translations.idiomatic: When matters touched army and state, they bit their tongues and held their peace.

sentences.zh: 徒摭不急之務，姑塞言責。

translations.literal: They merely picked up unurgent matters, simply to fill the duty to speak.
translations.idiomatic: They merely seized on trifling matters as a token fulfillment of their duty to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 延及數年，居然高踞卿貳，誇耀士林矣。

translations.literal: Extending over several years, they still sat high in secondary ministerial seats, boasting to the community of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After several years of this, they could still occupy high vice-ministerial posts and parade their standing before the scholarly world.

sentences.zh: 然此諸人豈盡矩詬無節，忍負陛下哉，亦有所懲而不敢耳。

translations.literal: Yet could these various men all be measured by the square and compass without propriety, bearing to fail Your Majesty? Rather, they had been punished and did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet were these men wholly without principle, willing to betray Your Majesty? No—they had been chastened and did not dare speak out.

sentences.zh: 如往歲傅應禎、艾穆、沈思孝、鄒元標皆以建言遠竄，至今與戍卒伍。

translations.literal: As in years past, Fu Yingzhen, Ai Mu, Shen Sixiao, and Zou Yuanbiao were all for memorializing exiled far away, down to the present serving in exile among garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In years past, Fu Yingzhen, Ai Mu, Shen Sixiao, and Zou Yuanbiao had all been banished to distant posts for their memorials, and to this day they remain among the ranks of exiled garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 此中才之士，所以內自顧恤，寧自同於寒蟬也。

translations.literal: For this reason men of talent within the court inwardly looked to themselves with care, preferring rather to be like the winter cicada.
translations.idiomatic: That is why talented men at court looked to their own safety and would rather remain silent as cicadas in winter.

sentences.zh: 宜特發德音，放還諸人，使天下曉然知聖天子無惡直言之意，則士皆慕義輸誠，效忠於陛下矣。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to issue a special gracious edict and release the various men to return, so that the realm clearly knows the sage Son of Heaven has no hatred of straight speech, then scholars will all admire righteousness and offer loyalty, serving Your Majesty with devotion."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should issue a special gracious decree recalling these men, so that all under heaven clearly knows the Son of Heaven bears no ill will toward candid speech—then scholars everywhere will be drawn to serve in earnest loyalty to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 居正欲重罪之。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng wished to punish him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng wished to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王國光曰：「罪之適成其名，請為公任怨。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Guoguang said: "Punishing him would only make his name; I beg to bear resentment on your behalf for the minister."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Guoguang said: "Punishing him would only enhance his reputation—let me bear the blame on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 遂出為楚府右長史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Right Administrator of the Chu princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon transferred out to serve as Right Administrator of the Chu princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 明年京察，復坐以不謹，落職歸。

translations.literal: The next year in the capital evaluation, he was again judged for lack of prudence, dismissed from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the capital evaluation of officials, he was again found remiss in duty and dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 居正死，起戶部郎中，出為陜西副使。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was reinstated as a Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent out as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng's death, he was reinstated as a director in the Ministry of Revenue and sent out as vice commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部右侍郎，督理倉場。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, supervising the granary depot.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, with responsibility for overseeing the capital granary depot.

sentences.zh: 世卿饒心計。

translations.literal: Shiqing was abundant in fiscal calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing was a skilled financial planner.

sentences.zh: 凡所條奏，酌劑贏縮，軍國賴焉。

translations.literal: In every item he memorialized, he balanced surplus and deficit; army and state relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In every policy he proposed, he carefully balanced revenues and expenditures, and both military and civil affairs depended on his judgment.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書陳有疾，侍郎張養蒙避不署事，帝怒，並罷之，而進世卿為尚書。

translations.literal: Revenue Minister Chen fell ill; Vice Minister Zhang Yangmeng avoided signing documents; the emperor was angered, dismissed both, and promoted Shiqing to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue Minister Chen fell ill and Vice Minister Zhang Yangmeng shirked his duties, the emperor's wrath fell on them both—they were dismissed, and Shiqing was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅使四出為害，江西稅監潘相至擅捕系宗室。

translations.literal: At the time mining-tax envoys went out in all directions doing harm; the Jiangxi tax supervisor Pan Xiang even on his own authority arrested and detained imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, mining-tax commissioners were spreading harm in every direction; the Jiangxi tax supervisor Pan Xiang went so far as to arrest and imprison members of the imperial clan on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 曩時關稅所入歲四十余萬，自為稅使所奪，商賈不行，數年間減三之一，四方雜課亦如之。

translations.literal: Formerly customs revenue yielded over four hundred thousand per year; once seized by tax envoys, merchants ceased to travel; within several years it was reduced by one-third, and miscellaneous levies throughout the realm were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Customs revenues had once brought in more than four hundred thousand taels annually; once the tax commissioners got their hands on them, commerce dried up, and within a few years revenue fell by a third; miscellaneous levies across the empire followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 歲入益寡，國用不支，邊儲告匱，而內供日繁。

translations.literal: Yearly income grew ever scarcer, state expenditure could not be met, frontier stores reported emptiness, while internal palace supply daily grew more lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenues dwindled ever further; the state treasury could not make ends meet; frontier stores were exhausted—while the palace's internal expenditures grew daily more extravagant.

sentences.zh: 歲增金花銀二十萬，宮帑日充羨。

translations.literal: Each year added two hundred thousand taels of patterned silver; the palace treasury daily overflowed with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The palace treasury received an additional two hundred thousand taels of patterned silver each year, and daily grew ever more flush.

sentences.zh: 世卿請復金花銀百萬故額，罷續增數，不許。

translations.literal: Shiqing requested restoring the former quota of one million taels of patterned silver and abolishing the continued increases—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing asked that the original quota of one million taels of patterned silver be restored and the continued increases abolished; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乞發內庫銀百萬及太仆馬價五十萬以濟邊儲，復忤旨切責。

translations.literal: He begged disbursing one million taels from the inner treasury and five hundred thousand in horse-price funds from the Court of the Imperial Stud to relieve frontier stores; again contrary to the emperor's will he was sternly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded for one million taels from the inner treasury plus five hundred thousand taels of horse funds from the Court of the Imperial Stud to replenish frontier stores—again defying the emperor's intent, he was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 世卿又請正潘相罪，且偕九卿數陳其害，皆不納。

translations.literal: Shiqing again requested rectifying Pan Xiang's guilt, and together with the Nine Ministers repeatedly stated the harms—all not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing again urged that Pan Xiang be punished according to law, and joined the Nine Ministers in repeatedly cataloguing the damage wrought by the tax commissioners—all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 世卿復言脂膏已竭，閭井蕭然，喪亂可虞，揭竿非遠，不及今罷之，恐後將無及。

translations.literal: Shiqing again said the fat and grease were already exhausted, lanes and wells desolate; disorder could be feared, raising poles was not far off—if not abolished now, he feared later there would be no reaching it in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing warned again that the people's substance was utterly drained, neighborhoods lay desolate, rebellion loomed on the horizon, and armed uprising was not far away—if the mining taxes were not abolished now, it might soon be too late.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不省。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，蘇、松稅監劉成以水災請暫停米稅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the Suzhou-Songjiang tax supervisor Liu Cheng requested temporarily suspending the rice tax on account of flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Wanli, Liu Cheng, the tax commissioner for Suzhou and Songjiang, requested a temporary suspension of the rice tax owing to flood damage.

sentences.zh: 帝以歲額六萬，米稅居半，不當盡停，今以四萬為額。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the annual quota was sixty thousand and the rice tax occupied half, held that it should not all be suspended; now set forty thousand as the quota.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that since the annual quota was sixty thousand taels and the rice tax accounted for half, a full suspension was unwarranted; he ordered that forty thousand taels remain as the quota.

sentences.zh: 世卿上言：「鄉者既免米稅，旋復再征，已失大信於天下。

translations.literal: Shiqing addressed the throne: "Formerly when the rice tax was already exempted, it was soon levied again—a great loss of trust to the realm already.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing memorialized: "Not long ago the rice tax was exempted, only to be levied again shortly afterward—we have already forfeited the empire's trust.

sentences.zh: 今成欲免稅額之半，而陛下不盡從，豈惻隱一念，貂榼尚存，而陛下反漠然不動心乎？」

translations.literal: Now Cheng wishes to exempt half the tax quota, yet Your Majesty does not fully follow—could it be that a thought of compassionate pity still survives in the fur cap and embroidered purse, yet Your Majesty on the contrary is indifferent and unmoved in heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Cheng asks to halve the tax quota, yet Your Majesty will not fully consent—does Your Majesty's compassionate impulse truly survive only in Liu Cheng's fur cap and purse, while Your Majesty himself remains utterly unmoved?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 其夏，雷火毀祖陵明樓，妖蟲蝕樹，又大雨壞神道橋梁。

translations.literal: That summer, thunder and fire destroyed the Bright Tower of the ancestral tombs; omens of insects ate the trees; again heavy rain ruined the spirit-way bridges.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, lightning set fire to the Bright Tower of the ancestral tombs; strange insects gnawed at the trees; torrential rains wrecked the bridges along the spirit way.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔咨實政。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict inquiring about solid governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict soliciting proposals for concrete reforms.

sentences.zh: 世卿上疏曰：

translations.literal: Shiqing submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 今日實政，孰有切於罷礦稅者！

translations.literal: Among solid governance today, what is more urgent than abolishing mining taxes!
translations.idiomatic: Of all the reforms needed today, what could be more urgent than abolishing the mining taxes!

sentences.zh: 古明主不貴異物，今也聚悖入之財，斂蒼生之怨，節儉之謂何？

translations.literal: Ancient enlightened rulers did not value strange objects; now gathering wealth of wrongful entry, gathering the resentment of the living masses—what is meant by frugality?
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened rulers of antiquity did not prize exotic luxuries—yet now the throne amasses ill-gotten wealth and harvests the people's resentment. Where is the frugality in that?

sentences.zh: 是為君德計，不可不罷者一。

translations.literal: Calculating for sovereign virtue, the first thing that must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of Your Majesty's moral standing, this is the first reason the mining taxes must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 多取所以招尤，慢藏必將誨盜。

translations.literal: Taking much therefore invites blame; treating stores lightly will teach theft.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive extraction invites reproach; careless hoarding inevitably teaches thieves.

sentences.zh: 鹿臺、鉅橋，足致倒戈之禍。

translations.literal: Lutai and Jubridge sufficed to bring the calamity of troops turning their blades.
translations.idiomatic: The Lutai Granary and Jubridge sufficed to bring down rulers by the swords of their own troops.

sentences.zh: 是為宗社計，不可不罷者二。

translations.literal: Calculating for altars of grain and soil, the second thing that must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the altars of state, this is the second reason they must go.

sentences.zh: 古者國家無事則預桑土之謀，有事則議金湯之策。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the state had no affairs it prepared mulberry-earth plans; when there were affairs it deliberated golden-soup strategies.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the realm was at peace the state attended to mulberry planting and flood control; when crisis came, it debated strategies of defense.

sentences.zh: 安有鑿四海之山，榷三家之市，操弓挾矢，戕及良民，毀室逾垣，禍延雞犬，經十數年而不休者！

translations.literal: How can there be drilling mountains throughout the four seas, monopolizing markets of three families, wielding bows and clutching arrows, harming good commoners, destroying rooms and crossing walls, calamity extending to chickens and dogs, passing ten-odd years without cease!
translations.idiomatic: What kingdom drills mines across the four seas, monopolizes every marketplace, sends armed men against innocent civilians, tears down houses and scales walls, spreads havoc even to barnyard fowl, and carries on thus for more than a decade without end!

sentences.zh: 是為國體計，不可不罷者三。

translations.literal: Calculating for the state's form, the third must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the dignity of the state, this is the third reason they must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 貂榼漁獵，翼虎咆哮。

translations.literal: Fur caps and purses plundered like fishing and hunting; winged tigers roared.
translations.idiomatic: The tax commissioners plundered like predators afield; backed by imperial authority, they roared like winged tigers.

sentences.zh: 毀掘冢墓，則枯骨蒙殃，奸虐子女，而良家飲恨。

translations.literal: Destroying and digging graves, then dry bones suffered calamity; violating and abusing sons and daughters, while good families nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They desecrated graves, bringing calamity even upon the dead; they violated women, leaving honorable families to choke on bitter rage.

sentences.zh: 人與為怨，讙噪屢聞，此而不已，後將何極！

translations.literal: Men all held resentment; clamor was often heard—if this does not cease, where afterward will it end!
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed with resentment; outcries were heard again and again—if this continues unchecked, where will it end!

sentences.zh: 是為民困計，不可不罷者四。

translations.literal: Calculating for the people's distress, the fourth must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the people's suffering, this is the fourth reason they must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 國家財賦不在民則在官，今盡括入奸人之室。

translations.literal: The state's finances and levies, if not with the people then with officials; now all were raked into the chambers of wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: The state's revenues belong either to the people or to the government—yet now they have all been scraped into the coffers of corrupt agents.

sentences.zh: 故督逋租而逋租絀，稽關稅而關稅虧，搜庫藏而庫藏絕，課鹽策而鹽策薄，征贖鍰而贖鍰消。

translations.literal: Therefore overseeing arrears in rent while rent arrears fell short, auditing customs duty while customs duty was deficient, searching storehouses while storehouses were exhausted, levying salt schemes while salt schemes were thin, collecting redemption fines while redemption fines vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Arrearage collection yielded fewer arrears; customs audits produced shrinking customs revenue; treasury searches left treasuries bare; salt levies grew ever thinner; fine collection dried up the fines themselves.

sentences.zh: 外府一空，司農若埽。

translations.literal: Outer treasuries were entirely empty; the Minister of Revenue was like swept ground.
translations.idiomatic: The outer treasuries stood utterly empty; the Ministry of Revenue was swept clean.

sentences.zh: 是為國課計，不可不罷者五。

translations.literal: Calculating for national levies, the fifth must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the national revenue, this is the fifth reason they must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 天子之令，信如四時。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's commands, trustworthy as the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor's word should be as dependable as the seasons.

sentences.zh: 三載前嘗曰「朕心仁愛，自有停止之時」，今年復一年，更待何日？

translations.literal: Three years before he once said "My heart is benevolent and loving; there will naturally be a time to stop"—now another year passes, awaiting what day?
translations.idiomatic: Three years ago Your Majesty declared, "My heart is compassionate; there will come a time to end this"—yet another year has passed; how much longer must we wait?

sentences.zh: 天子有戲言，王命委草莽。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven has jesting words, royal commands are cast to the wild grass.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor's words are idle jest, his decrees are discarded like trash.

sentences.zh: 是為詔令計，不可不罷者六。

translations.literal: Calculating for edicts and orders, the sixth must be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of imperial credibility, this is the sixth reason they must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 陛下試思：服食宮室，以至營造征討，上何事不取之民，民何事不供之上？

translations.literal: Your Majesty try thinking: food and clothing, palace rooms, extending to construction and punitive campaigns—what affair above does not take from the people, what affair below do the people not supply above?
translations.idiomatic: Consider, Your Majesty: from food and clothing and palace maintenance to construction projects and military campaigns—what does the throne not take from the people, and what do the people not supply to the throne?

sentences.zh: 嗟此赤子，曾無負於國，乃民方歡呼以供九重之欲，而陛下不少遂其欲；

translations.literal: Alas these newborn children, never having failed the state—yet the people just now shout with joy to supply the ninefold gate's desires, while Your Majesty does not slightly satisfy their desires;
translations.idiomatic: Alas for these innocent common folk, who have never wronged the state—the people strain willingly to satisfy the palace's every desire, yet Your Majesty will not grant them the least satisfaction in return;

sentences.zh: 民方奔走以供九重之勞，而陛下不少慰其勞；

translations.literal: The people just now run about to supply the ninefold gate's toil, while Your Majesty does not slightly comfort their toil;
translations.idiomatic: the people toil eagerly to bear the palace's burdens, yet Your Majesty offers them no comfort for their labors;

sentences.zh: 民方竭蹶以赴九重之難，而陛下不少恤其難。

translations.literal: The people just now exhaust their limbs to rush to the ninefold gate's hardship, while Your Majesty does not slightly pity their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: the people exhaust themselves in hardship on the throne's behalf, yet Your Majesty shows them no compassion for their suffering.

sentences.zh: 返之於心，必有不自安者矣。

translations.literal: Returning it to the heart, there must be something not self-at-ease.
translations.idiomatic: Turned inward upon the heart, there must be discomfort.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿謂蠢蠢小民可駕馭自我，生殺自我，而不足介意也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty do not say the dumbly stirring small people can be driven and controlled by self, life and death by self, and are not worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not suppose that these humble commoners can be driven at will, that their lives and deaths are entirely in your hands, and that they are beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 民之心既天之心，今天譴頻仍，雷火妖蟲，淫雨疊至，變不虛生，其應非遠。

translations.literal: The people's heart is already Heaven's heart; now Heaven's reproaches come repeatedly—thunder, fire, omens of insects, excessive rain arriving in layers—transformations are not born in emptiness; their responses are not far.
translations.idiomatic: The hearts of the people are the heart of Heaven—and Heaven's reproaches now come thick and fast: thunder and fire, strange insects, torrents of rain one upon another. Omens are not sent without cause; retribution cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 故今日欲回天意在恤民心，欲恤民心在罷礦稅，無煩再計而決者。

translations.literal: Therefore today to wish to turn back Heaven's intent lies in comforting the people's hearts; to wish to comfort the people's hearts lies in abolishing mining taxes—no need again to calculate and decide.
translations.idiomatic: To win back Heaven's favor today, Your Majesty must comfort the people's hearts—and to comfort the people's hearts, you must abolish the mining taxes. The decision requires no further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 帝優答之，而不行。

translations.literal: The emperor answered graciously, but did not implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with gracious words but took no action.

sentences.zh: 至三十四年三月，始詔罷礦使，稅亦稍減。

translations.literal: By the thirty-fourth year third month, he first decreed abolishing mining envoys; taxes also slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the third month of the thirty-fourth year did he issue a decree abolishing the mining commissioners; taxes were also somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 然遼東、雲南、四川稅使自若，吏民尤苦之。

translations.literal: Yet Liaodong, Yunnan, and Sichuan tax envoys remained as before; officials and people suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Liaodong, Yunnan, and Sichuan the tax commissioners remained in place, and officials and commoners suffered all the more.

sentences.zh: 雲南遂變作，楊榮被戕。

translations.literal: Yunnan then erupted in revolt; Yang Rong was slain.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan then broke into rebellion, and Yang Rong was killed.

sentences.zh: 而西北水旱時時見告，世卿屢請減租發振，國用益不支。

translations.literal: Meanwhile in the northwest flood and drought were reported from time to time; Shiqing repeatedly requested reducing rents and disbursing relief; state expenditure increasingly could not be met.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the northwest suffered repeated reports of flood and drought; Shiqing repeatedly pleaded for rent reductions and famine relief—but state finances grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 逾月復奏請捐內帑百萬佐軍用，不從。

translations.literal: After a month he again memorialized requesting donating one million from the inner purse to assist military expenditure—not followed.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he again memorialized asking that one million taels from the inner treasury be contributed toward military expenses; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 世卿遂連章求去，至十五上，竟不許。

translations.literal: Shiqing then submitted successive memorials requesting to leave, reaching fifteen times—all not permitted in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing then submitted memorial after memorial requesting retirement—fifteen in all—yet each was denied.

sentences.zh: 先是，福王將婚，進部帑二十七萬，帝猶以為少，數遣中使趣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Fu was about to marry, two hundred seventy thousand from ministry funds was submitted; the emperor still thought it too little, repeatedly sending eunuch envoys to press for more.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Prince of Fu's wedding was being arranged, the ministry contributed two hundred seventy thousand taels—but the emperor still considered it insufficient and repeatedly sent eunuchs to demand more.

sentences.zh: 中使出誶語，且劾世卿抗命。

translations.literal: Eunuch envoys spoke abusive words, and moreover impeached Shiqing for resisting orders.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs uttered insults and even impeached Shiqing for defying orders.

sentences.zh: 世卿以為辱國，疏聞於朝，帝置不問。

translations.literal: Shiqing considered it a disgrace to the state, memorialized informing the court; the emperor set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing regarded this as a national disgrace and memorialized the court; the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 至三十六年，七公主下嫁，宣索至數十萬。

translations.literal: By the thirty-sixth year, when the seventh princess married down, an edict demanded reaching several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirty-sixth year, when the seventh princess was given in marriage, the palace demanded several hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 世卿引故事力爭，詔減三之一。

translations.literal: Shiqing cited precedent and contended forcefully; an edict reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing cited precedent and argued forcefully; an edict cut the sum by one-third.

sentences.zh: 世卿復言：「陛下大婚止七萬，長公主下嫁止十二萬，乞陛下再裁損，一仿長公主例。」

translations.literal: Shiqing again said: "Your Majesty's great wedding stopped at seventy thousand, the eldest princess marrying down stopped at one hundred twenty thousand—I beg Your Majesty again trim and reduce, entirely following the eldest princess precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing pressed further: "Your Majesty's own grand wedding cost only seventy thousand taels, and the eldest princess's dowry totaled only one hundred twenty thousand—I beg Your Majesty to cut the sum again, following the eldest princess's precedent."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已從之。

translations.literal: The emperor with no alternative followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no choice, acceded.

sentences.zh: 福王新出府第，設崇文稅店，爭民利，世卿亦諫阻。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu newly left his princely residence, established a Chongwen tax shop, competing for people's profit—Shiqing also remonstrated and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu newly established his household outside the palace, he opened a Chongwen tax shop to compete with commoners for profit—Shiqing remonstrated against this as well.

sentences.zh: 世卿素勵清操，當官盡職。

translations.literal: Shiqing from of old encouraged pure integrity; holding office he fulfilled duty entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing had long cultivated personal integrity and fulfilled his duties conscientiously in office.

sentences.zh: 帝雅重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him by longstanding custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 吏部缺尚書，嘗使兼署，推舉無所私。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister, he was often made to concurrently administer; in recommendations he had nothing private.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister, the emperor often had him serve in that capacity as well; in personnel recommendations he showed no partiality.

sentences.zh: 惟楚宗人與王相訐，世卿力言王非偽，與沈一貫議合。

translations.literal: Only when Chu clansmen and the prince mutually accused, Shiqing argued forcefully the prince was not false, agreeing with Shen Yiguan's view.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the affair where Chu clansmen and the prince traded accusations did Shiqing insist forcefully that the prince was genuine, aligning with Shen Yiguan's position.

sentences.zh: 李廷機輔政，世卿力推之。

translations.literal: When Li Tingji assisted in government, Shiqing forcefully promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tingji served as grand secretary, Shiqing vigorously supported his appointment.

sentences.zh: 廷臣遂疑世卿黨比。

translations.literal: Court ministers then suspected Shiqing of factional alignment.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials then suspected Shiqing of factional allegiance.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中杜士全、鄧去霄、何士晉、胡忻，御史蘇為霖、馬孟禎等先後劾之，世卿遂杜門乞去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretaries Du Shiquan, Deng Quxiao, He Shijin, and Hu Xin, Censor Su Weilin, Ma Mengzhen, and others in succession impeached him; Shiqing then closed his doors begging to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon supervising secretaries Du Shiquan, Deng Quxiao, He Shijin, and Hu Xin, along with censors Su Weilin and Ma Mengzhen, impeached him in succession; Shiqing then shut his doors and petitioned for retirement.

sentences.zh: 章復十余上，不報。

translations.literal: Memorials again over ten times submitted—no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten further memorials—all without response.

sentences.zh: 三十八年秋，世卿乃拜疏出城候命。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year autumn, Shiqing then bowed with his memorial and left the city awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirty-eighth year, Shiqing formally submitted his memorial and left the capital to await the emperor's reply.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，乘柴車徑去。

translations.literal: The next year in the tenth month, he rode a firewood cart and went straight away.
translations.idiomatic: The following October, he departed directly in a humble ox cart.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以聞，帝亦不罪也。

translations.literal: The court ministers reported it on; the Emperor also did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials reported the matter, but the Emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 家居七年卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Living at home seven years he died; was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for seven years and then died; he was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 李汝華，字茂夫，睢州人。

translations.literal: Li Ruhua, style Maofu, a man of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua, whose style name was Maofu, came from Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授兗州推官。

translations.literal: Was appointed investigating magistrate of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 征授工科給事中，嘗劾戎政尚書鄭洛不職。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Works section; once impeached Minister of Military Administration Zheng Luo for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to the capital he was appointed a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works, and once impeached Zheng Luo, Minister of Military Administration, for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 及出閱甘肅邊務，洛方經略西事，主和戎。

translations.literal: When he went out to inspect Gansu border affairs, Luo was just managing western matters, advocating peace with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent to inspect border affairs in Gansu, Zheng Luo was then directing western frontier policy and advocating appeasement of the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 汝華疏洛畏敵貽患，且劾諸將吏侵軍資，復請盡墾甘肅閑田。

translations.literal: Ruhua memorialized that Luo feared the enemy and bequeathed trouble; moreover impeached various generals and officials for encroaching on military funds, and again requested fully reclaiming Gansu's idle fields.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua memorialized that Zheng Luo's fear of the enemy would invite lasting harm, impeached various commanders and officials for embezzling military funds, and also petitioned for the full reclamation of unused farmland in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 還朝，歷吏科都給事中，多所糾擿。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he served successively as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Secretariat section, and often impeached and exposed others.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he rose to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Secretariat section, where he frequently impeached and exposed officials.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常少卿，擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Grand Coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 稅使四出，議括關津諸稅輸內府。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners went out in all directions; it was proposed to gather checkpoint and ferry taxes and deliver them to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioners were dispatched throughout the empire, and there was a proposal to collect customs duties at checkpoints and ferry stations and turn them over to the inner palace treasury.

sentences.zh: 汝華以稅本餉軍，力爭止之。

translations.literal: Ruhua held that taxes were originally to provision armies, and forcefully argued to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua argued forcefully that tax revenues were meant to provision the army and pressed to stop the scheme.

sentences.zh: 既而詔四方稅務盡領於有司，以其半輸稅監，進內府，半輸戶部。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered tax affairs in all quarters to be fully overseen by regular officials; half was to be delivered to tax commissioners and enter the inner palace, half to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered that tax administration throughout the empire be placed under local civil officials, with half the revenue remitted to the tax commissioners for the inner palace and half to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 獨江西潘相勒有司悉由己輸。

translations.literal: Only in Jiangxi, Pan Xiang urged the officials that all should be delivered through himself.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Jiangxi did the tax commissioner Pan Xiang pressure local officials to remit all revenues through him alone.

sentences.zh: 汝華極論相違詔，帝竟如相議，且推行之四方。

translations.literal: Ruhua argued extremely that Xiang violated the edict; the Emperor finally followed Xiang's proposal, and moreover extended it to the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua argued strenuously that Pan Xiang was defying the edict, but the Emperor ultimately adopted Pan's arrangement and extended it throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 汝華在贛十四年，威惠甚著，進秩兵部右侍郎，召拜戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Ruhua was in Gan fourteen years; authority and kindness were very prominent; advanced in rank to Right Vice Minister of War, summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua served fourteen years in Ganzhou, winning great renown through his authority and benevolence; he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and then summoned to serve as Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙世卿去位，遂掌部事。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Shiqing left his post; he then managed the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Zhao Shiqing left office, Li Ruhua took charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 福王莊田四萬頃，詔旨屢趣，不能及額。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was granted forty thousand qing of estate fields; edict-orders repeatedly urged fulfillment, yet the quota could not be met.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts repeatedly pressed for the allocation of forty thousand qing of estate land to the Prince of Fu, but the quota could not be met.

sentences.zh: 汝華數偕廷臣執爭，僅減四之一。

translations.literal: Ruhua several times together with court ministers stubbornly contended; only reduced by one of four.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua joined other court officials in repeated adamant protests, securing only a reduction of one quarter.

sentences.zh: 及王既之國，詔許自遣使督租，所在驛騷。

translations.literal: When the prince had already gone to his fief, an edict permitted him to dispatch envoys himself to supervise rent; wherever they went, post stations were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince had departed for his fief, an edict allowed him to dispatch his own agents to collect rents, throwing post stations everywhere into uproar.

sentences.zh: 內使閻時詣汝州，杖二人死。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yan Shi went to Ruzhou and clubbed two men to death.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yan Shi went to Ruzhou and beat two men to death.

sentences.zh: 汝華請遵祖制隸有司，盡撤還使者，不納。

translations.literal: Ruhua requested following ancestral regulations to subject princely estates to regular officials, fully withdrawing and returning the envoys—not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua petitioned that princely rent collection be placed under civil officials as ancestral law prescribed and that all rent-collecting agents be withdrawn, but his proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 畿輔、山東大饑，因汝華言，出倉米平糶，且發銀以振。

translations.literal: The capital region and Shandong suffered great famine; on account of Ruhua's words, granary rice was released at fair sale, and silver was also disbursed for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region and Shandong suffered severe famine, at Li Ruhua's urging the government released grain from state granaries for sale at fair prices and disbursed silver for relief.

sentences.zh: 汝華復奏行救荒數事，兩地賴之。

translations.literal: Ruhua again memorialized implementing several famine-relief measures; both regions relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua further memorialized implementing several famine-relief measures, on which both regions depended.

sentences.zh: 先是，山東饑，蠲歲賦七十萬。

translations.literal: Before this, when Shandong suffered famine, annual levies of seven hundred thousand were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shandong had suffered famine, annual land taxes totaling seven hundred thousand taels had been remitted.

sentences.zh: 是年盡蠲又百七十余萬。

translations.literal: That year a complete remission was again more than one million seven hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That year full remissions amounted to more than 1.7 million taels in addition.

sentences.zh: 汝華以邊餉不繼，請天下稅課未入內藏者，暫留一年補其缺，輔臣亦助為言。

translations.literal: Ruhua, because border provisions were not continuing, requested that throughout the empire tax levies not yet entered the inner storehouse be temporarily retained one year to fill the gap; assisting ministers also helped speak for it.
translations.idiomatic: With frontier military pay falling short, Li Ruhua requested that tax revenues not yet transferred to the inner palace treasury be held for one year to make up the shortfall; senior ministers also spoke in support.

sentences.zh: 疏三上，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was thrice submitted; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial three times without receiving a reply.

sentences.zh: 已，進尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly after, advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly thereafter promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，鄭繼之去，兼攝吏部事。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, Zheng Jizhi departed; he concurrently managed Ministry of Personnel affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Wanli, when Zheng Jizhi left office, Li Ruhua also took charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 畿輔、陜西大饑，汝華請振，皆不報。

translations.literal: The capital region and Shaanxi suffered great famine; Ruhua requested relief—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region and Shaanxi again suffered severe famine, Li Ruhua petitioned for relief but received no response.

sentences.zh: 遼東兵事興，驟增餉三百萬。

translations.literal: Liaodong military affairs arose; provisions suddenly increased by three million.
translations.idiomatic: With war breaking out in Liaodong, military pay was suddenly increased by three million taels.

sentences.zh: 汝華累請發內帑不得，則借支南京部帑，括天下庫藏余積，征宿逋，裁工食，開事例。

translations.literal: Ruhua repeatedly requested disbursing the inner treasury and could not obtain it; then borrowed from the Nanjing ministry treasury, gathered remaining accumulations of treasuries throughout the empire, levied long-standing arrears, cut worker rations, and opened offices for sale of precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua repeatedly petitioned for disbursements from the inner palace treasury without success; he then drew advances from the Nanjing ministry treasury, swept up surplus reserves from treasuries across the empire, collected long-standing arrears, cut workers' rations, and opened offices selling official titles and privileges.

sentences.zh: 而遼東巡撫周永春請益兵加賦，汝華議：天下田賦，自貴州外，畝增銀三厘五毫，得餉二百萬。

translations.literal: Moreover the Liaodong Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun requested increased troops and increased levies; Ruhua proposed: throughout the empire field levies, outside Guizhou, increase per mu by three li five hao of silver, obtaining provisions of two million.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun requested more troops and higher taxes, Li Ruhua proposed adding three li five hao of silver per mu to land taxes empire-wide except Guizhou, raising two million taels in military pay.

sentences.zh: 明年，復議益兵增賦如前。

translations.literal: The next year, again deliberated increasing troops and increasing levies as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the same proposal for more troops and higher taxes was debated again.

sentences.zh: 又明年四月，兵部以募兵市馬，工部以制器，再議增賦。

translations.literal: Again the next year, fourth month: the Ministry of War because of recruiting troops and buying horses, the Ministry of Works because of making weapons—again deliberated increased levies.
translations.idiomatic: In April of the year after that, the Ministry of War sought funds to recruit troops and purchase horses and the Ministry of Works to manufacture weapons, and tax increases were debated once more.

sentences.zh: 於是畝增二厘，為銀百二十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon per mu increased two li, making silver one million two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A further two li per mu was added, yielding 1.2 million taels.

sentences.zh: 先後三增賦，凡五百二十萬有奇，遂為歲額。

translations.literal: Before and after three increased levies, altogether five million two hundred thousand odd, thus becoming the annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Three tax increases in succession totaled a little more than 5.2 million taels, which then became the permanent annual levy.

sentences.zh: 當是時，內帑山積，廷臣請發，率不應。

translations.literal: At that time the inner treasury piled like mountains; court ministers requested disbursing—generally no response.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the inner palace treasury overflowed with accumulated wealth, yet when court officials petitioned for disbursements, the Emperor almost never agreed.

sentences.zh: 計臣無如何，遂為一切茍且之計，苛斂百姓。

translations.literal: The planning minister had nothing to do about it; thereupon adopted every expedient makeshift plan, harshly levying the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Revenue could do nothing else and resorted to every stopgap measure, squeezing harsh levies from the people.

sentences.zh: 而樞臣征兵，乃遠及蠻方，致奢崇明、安邦彥相繼反，用師連年。

translations.literal: Moreover the chief minister conscripted troops, reaching far to the barbarian regions, causing She Chongming and An Bangyan successively to rebel, employing troops year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the chief minister's conscription drives reached deep into the frontier, provoking She Chongming and An Bangyan to rebel in succession and keeping armies in the field year after year.

sentences.zh: 又割四川、雲南、廣西、湖廣、廣東所加之賦以餉之，而遼餉仍不充，天下已不可支矣。

translations.literal: Moreover cut from Sichuan, Yunnan, Guangxi, Huguang, and Guangdong the added levies to provision them; yet Liaodong provisions still were not filled—the empire already could not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Revenues from the tax increases in Sichuan, Yunnan, Guangxi, Huguang, and Guangdong were diverted to feed these campaigns, yet Liaodong military pay remained insufficient and the empire could no longer bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 汝華練達勤敏，立朝無黨阿。

translations.literal: Ruhua was practiced and penetrating, diligent and quick; standing at court without factional flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua was seasoned, diligent, and capable, and stood above factional flattery at court.

sentences.zh: 官戶部久，於國計贏縮，邊儲虛實，與鹽漕屯牧諸大政，皆殫心裁劑。

translations.literal: Serving as Minister of Revenue long, regarding state planning surplus and deficit, border storage empty and full, together with salt transport, garrison agriculture, and other great policies—all exhaustively minded and judged.
translations.idiomatic: During his long tenure at the Ministry of Revenue he devoted himself fully to fiscal surplus and deficit, the strength of frontier granaries, and major policies governing the salt monopoly, grain transport, and garrison agriculture.

sentences.zh: 歲比不登，意常主寬恤，獨加賦之議不能力持，馴致萬方虛耗，內外交訌。

translations.literal: Year after year harvests did not succeed; his intent always advocated lenient relief, only the proposal of increased levies he could not strongly hold; gradually leading to exhaustion throughout all directions, inner and outer crossing in conflict.
translations.idiomatic: When harvests failed year after year he consistently favored relief and leniency, but he could not hold firm against the tax-increase proposals, and gradually the realm was drained dry and beset by turmoil within and without.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年得疾乞休，加太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he fell ill and requested retirement; was granted Senior Tutor of the Crown Prince and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianqi reign he fell ill and petitioned to retire; he was granted the title Senior Tutor of the Crown Prince and allowed to resign.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚恭敏。

translations.literal: Died; posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Gongmin, "Respectful and Diligent."

sentences.zh: 從子夢辰，自有傳。

translations.literal: His nephew Mengchen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li Mengchen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：古稱文昌政本，七卿之任，蓋其重矣。

translations.literal: Appraisal: In antiquity they called civil administration the root of government; the responsibilities of the Seven Ministers—probably their weight is so.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: The ancients called civil administration the foundation of government; the responsibilities borne by the Seven Ministers were indeed weighty.

sentences.zh: 萬士和諸人奉職勤慮，異夫依阿保位之流；

translations.literal: Wan Shihe and the rest served office with diligent consideration, different from the sort who rely on flattery to preserve position;
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shihe and his colleagues served with conscientious diligence, unlike those who clung to office through sycophantic compliance;

sentences.zh: 劉應節、王遴、舒化、李世達尤其卓然者哉。

translations.literal: Liu Yingjie, Wang Lin, Shu Hua, Li Shida—especially the outstanding ones indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yingjie, Wang Lin, Shu Hua, and Li Shida were especially outstanding among them.

sentences.zh: 李汝華司邦計，值兵興餉絀，請帑不應，乃不能以去就爭，而權宜取濟，遂與裒刻聚斂者同譏。

translations.literal: Li Ruhua managed state finances, encountering military rise and provisions shortage, requesting treasury disbursements without response; then unable to contend by departure and retention, but expediently finding relief, thus together with those who gather and carve out levies received the same reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhua managed the national finances at a time when war had broken out and military funds ran short; his petitions for treasury disbursements went unanswered, and unable to stake his career on the issue, he turned to expedients that left him condemned alongside the harsh tax collectors.

sentences.zh: 時事至此，其可嘆也夫！

translations.literal: Affairs reaching this point—how lamentable indeed!
translations.idiomatic: That matters had come to such a pass—how lamentable!
